motion.name: BoxShadowMotionValue
motion.documentation:
A [MotionValue] holding an animatable list of [BoxShadow]s, or `null` for
"no shadow".

motion.name: ColorMotionValue
motion.documentation:
A [MotionValue] holding an animatable background color, or `null` for
"no color".

motion.name: ComputedMotionValue
motion.documentation:
A read-only [MotionValue] computed from any number of dependencies.

Unlike [DerivedMotionValue] (one source, eager), a `ComputedMotionValue`
depends on several [Listenable]s — typically other [MotionValue]s, but
scroll positions, animation controllers and notifiers work too — and is
**lazy**:

* When a dependency changes the value is only marked stale and its own
  listeners are notified; [compute] runs the next time [value] is read
  (in practice: at paint time, after every dependency has finished
  updating). In a diamond-shaped graph (`a → b`, `a → c`, `d = f(b, c)`)
  a render object reading `d` at paint therefore sees `b` and `c` both
  updated. A listener that reads `d` *synchronously while `a` is still
  notifying* can still observe an eager [DerivedMotionValue] intermediate;
  read in paint/layout, or after the update that triggered the change.
* Dependencies must exist before the computed value, so cycles cannot be
  constructed; no cycle detection is needed.

[velocity] is `0`: a computed value has no closed-form derivative. Use
[MotionValueMapRange.mapRange] when velocity must flow through a mapping.

Assigning to [value] or calling [update] throws a [StateError].

members.name: ComputedMotionValue
members.documentation:
Creates a value that evaluates [compute] whenever it is read after one of
[dependencies] has changed.

members.name: compute
members.documentation: Computes the current value from the dependencies.

motion.name: DerivedMotionValue
motion.documentation:
A [MotionValue] whose value is computed from a source [MotionValue].

Created via [MotionValue.transform] or [MotionValueMapRange.mapRange].
Whenever the source value changes, [mapper] is re-applied and the result
is written to this value (which in turn notifies its own listeners only
if the mapped result actually changed).

Because a `DerivedMotionValue` is itself a [MotionValue], it can be
chained: `source.transform(...).transform(...)`.

members.name: DerivedMotionValue
members.documentation:
Creates a value derived from `source` by applying [mapper].

If [velocityMapper] is given it converts the source's `(value, velocity)`
into this value's velocity (e.g. `mapRange` multiplies by the segment
slope); otherwise the derived velocity is `0`.

members.name: mapper
members.documentation: The function applied to the source value to produce this value.

members.name: velocityMapper
members.signature: final double Function(S value, double velocity)? velocityMapper
members.documentation: Maps the source's value and velocity to this value's velocity.

motion.name: DismissDirection
motion.documentation:
The axis (and, for horizontal/vertical, the allowed direction) a
[NibSwipeDismiss] can be swiped in.

members.name: horizontal
members.documentation: Swiping left or right both trigger dismissal.

members.name: vertical
members.documentation: Swiping up or down both trigger dismissal.

members.name: startToEnd
members.documentation:
Only swiping left-to-right (i.e. a positive horizontal offset)
triggers dismissal.

members.name: endToStart
members.documentation:
Only swiping right-to-left (i.e. a negative horizontal offset)
triggers dismissal.

motion.name: InertiaSolver
motion.documentation:
Drives a [MotionValue<double>] with a decelerating "coast to a stop"
simulation, using the same friction model iOS uses for scroll
deceleration.

`InertiaSolver` runs a [flutter_physics.FrictionSimulation] on a [Ticker]
and writes the simulated position to [value] on every tick, the same
pattern `SpringSolver` uses.

members.name: InertiaSolver
members.documentation:
Creates a solver that decelerates [value] from its current position,
ticking via a [Ticker] obtained from [vsync].

members.name: drag
members.documentation:
The friction coefficient used for subsequent [animateTo] calls. Values
closer to `1.0` coast farther before stopping; `0.135` matches the
deceleration rate iOS uses for scrolling.

members.name: onComplete
members.documentation: Called when the running simulation settles within tolerance.

members.name: boundsSpring
members.documentation:
The spring that pulls the value back to a bound it overshot. Defaults to
a critically-damped-ish spring that feels like a scroll view bounce.

members.name: animateTo
members.signature: Future<void> animateTo({required double velocity, double? min, double? max})
members.documentation:
Starts a deceleration simulation from the current [MotionValue]
position with the given initial [velocity], in units per second.

With [min] and/or [max], the value is elastically bounded: if the
coast would cross a bound it overshoots it and springs back (using
[boundsSpring]), coming to rest exactly on the bound. A value that
starts outside the bounds springs back to the nearest one.

The returned future completes when the value comes to rest, or when the
animation is superseded by another [animateTo] or by [stop]/[dispose].

members.name: stop
members.documentation:
Stops the simulation immediately, freezing [value] at its current
position. [MotionValue.velocity] is left intact so a driver that takes
over continues the motion; the pending [animateTo] future completes.

members.name: dispose
members.documentation:
Stops and disposes the underlying [Ticker]. Safe to call whether or not
an animation is running.

motion.name: MotionConverter
motion.documentation:
Splits a value type into independent scalar channels so each channel can be
driven by its own physics, and joins the channels back.

`Offset(dx, dy)` is two channels; a spring toward a new `Offset` moves `dx`
and `dy` with *independent* positions and velocities, exactly as two
separate scalar springs would, but writes one composed value.

members.name: MotionConverter
members.documentation: Const constructor for subclasses.

members.name: MotionConverter.custom
members.documentation:
Creates a converter from closures, for types NibMotion does not know.

[normalize] must return exactly [channels] numbers and [denormalize]
must accept a list of that length.

members.name: scalar
members.documentation: A plain scalar (one channel).

members.name: offset
members.documentation: `Offset` as `[dx, dy]`.

members.name: size
members.documentation: `Size` as `[width, height]`.

members.name: rect
members.documentation: `Rect` as `[left, top, right, bottom]`.

members.name: alignment
members.documentation: `Alignment` as `[x, y]`.

members.name: edgeInsets
members.documentation: `EdgeInsets` as `[left, top, right, bottom]`.

members.name: color
members.documentation:
`Color` as `[alpha, red, green, blue]` in `0..1`. Springs that overshoot
are clamped back into range when the colour is rebuilt.

members.name: maybeFor
members.documentation: The built-in converter for [T], or `null` if there is none.

members.name: channels
members.documentation: How many scalar channels [T] is split into.

members.name: normalize
members.documentation: Splits [value] into [channels] numbers.

members.name: denormalize
members.documentation: Rebuilds a [T] from [channels] numbers.

motion.name: MotionValue
motion.documentation:
A reactive container for a single animatable value of type [T].

`MotionValue` is the core primitive that animation drivers (such as
[SpringSolver]) write to and that `RenderNibMotion` listens to in order to
repaint directly via `markNeedsPaint()`. Setting [value] notifies
listeners exactly once per distinct change — no widget rebuilds occur as
a result.

members.name: MotionValue
members.documentation:
Creates a [MotionValue] holding [initial] as its starting value.
A `double` initial value must be finite.

members.name: velocity
members.documentation:
The instantaneous rate of change of this value, in units per second.

Animation drivers ([SpringSolver], [InertiaSolver], tweens) publish
their velocity through [update], and a new driver starts from it, so an
interrupted animation hands its momentum to whatever takes over instead
of restarting from rest. Plain assignment to [value] is a *jump* and
resets the velocity to `0`. Always `0` for non-numeric values.

members.name: value
members.documentation:
Updates the current value.

If [newValue] is equal to the current value, listeners are not
notified. Otherwise the value is replaced and [ChangeNotifier]
listeners are notified synchronously.

members.name: update
members.documentation:
Sets [value] and records [velocity] (units per second) alongside it.

Listeners are notified only when the value itself changes. Used by
animation drivers so momentum survives interruption; see [velocity].

members.name: hasListeners
members.documentation:
Whether this value currently has any listeners attached.

The inherited `ChangeNotifier.hasListeners` is `@protected`; this
override makes it public so derived values and tests can verify
listener wiring (e.g. that disposing a [DerivedMotionValue] removes its
listener from its source).

members.name: computed
members.signature:
static ComputedMotionValue<R> computed<R>(
    List<Listenable> dependencies,
    R Function() compute,
  )
members.documentation:
Creates a lazy, glitch-free [ComputedMotionValue] that re-evaluates
[compute] after any of [dependencies] changes.

```dart
final scale = MotionValue.computed(
    [progress, boost], () => 0.9 + progress.value * boost.value);
```

members.name: transform
members.signature: DerivedMotionValue<T, R> transform<R>(R Function(T value) mapper)
members.documentation:
Creates a [DerivedMotionValue] that tracks `mapper(value)`.

The derived value recomputes (and notifies its own listeners) whenever
this value changes. The returned value is itself a [MotionValue], so
`transform` calls can be chained.

motion.name: MotionValueMapRange
motion.documentation: Adds [mapRange] to numeric [MotionValue]s.

members.name: mapRange
members.documentation:
Creates a [DerivedMotionValue] that linearly maps this value from
[inputRange] to [outputRange].

[inputRange] and [outputRange] are parallel lists: `inputRange[i]`
corresponds to `outputRange[i]`. At least two finite stops are required;
input stops must be strictly increasing. The stop lists are copied.
Between stops, the result is linearly interpolated. When [clamp] is
true (the default), values outside [inputRange] are clamped to the
nearest end of [outputRange]; otherwise the first/last segment's slope
is extrapolated.

motion.name: MultiSpringSolver
motion.documentation:
Drives a [MotionValue] of a composite type (`Offset`, `Size`, `Color`, …)
with one spring **per channel**, so each axis keeps its own position and
velocity.

Retargeting mid-flight starts every channel from its current position and
current velocity (per-axis momentum hand-off). A value that was assigned
from outside since the last tick counts as a jump: velocities reset to `0`.

One [Ticker] drives all channels and the composed value is written (and
listeners notified) once per frame.

members.name: MultiSpringSolver
members.signature:
MultiSpringSolver({
    required TickerProvider vsync,
    required MotionValue<T> value,
    required this.converter,
    required this.spring,
    this.onComplete,
  })
members.documentation: Creates a solver for [value] using [converter] to split it into channels.

members.name: converter
members.documentation: Splits [T] into scalar channels.

members.name: spring
members.documentation: The spring used by subsequent [animateTo] calls (applied to every channel).

members.name: onComplete
members.documentation: Called when all channels have settled naturally.

members.name: velocities
members.documentation: Current per-channel velocities, in channel units per second.

members.name: isAnimating
members.documentation: Whether a spring is currently running.

members.name: animateTo
members.documentation:
Springs every channel toward [target].

[initialVelocity] (one number per channel) overrides the inherited
per-channel velocity. With [immediate] the value jumps to [target] with
zero velocity (used for reduced motion).

The returned future completes when all channels settle, or when this
animation is superseded by another [animateTo] or by [stop]/[dispose].

members.name: stop
members.documentation:
Freezes the value where it is. Per-channel velocities are kept for a
following [animateTo]; the pending future completes.

members.name: dispose
members.documentation: Stops and disposes the ticker. Safe to call more than once.

motion.name: NibAnim
motion.documentation:
An immutable snapshot of every visual property `NibMotion` can animate.

Each property is nullable: `null` means "this animation does not touch
this property" rather than "set this property to zero/identity". During
[lerp], a `null` value on one side falls back to the corresponding
[identity] value so animations only affect the properties the caller
actually specifies.

members.name: NibAnim
members.signature:
const NibAnim({
    this.x,
    this.y,
    this.scale,
    this.scaleX,
    this.scaleY,
    this.rotate,
    this.skewX,
    this.skewY,
    this.rotateX,
    this.rotateY,
    this.blur,
    this.tint,
    this.opacity,
    this.color,
    this.borderRadius,
    this.boxShadow,
  })
members.documentation:
Creates an animation snapshot. Any omitted property is left untouched
by this animation.

members.name: x
members.documentation: Horizontal offset from the widget's natural position, in pixels.

members.name: y
members.documentation: Vertical offset from the widget's natural position, in pixels.

members.name: scale
members.documentation: Uniform scale applied to both axes. Identity is `1.0`.

members.name: scaleX
members.documentation: Horizontal scale. Identity is `1.0`.

members.name: scaleY
members.documentation: Vertical scale. Identity is `1.0`.

members.name: rotate
members.documentation: Rotation around the Z axis, in turns (`1.0` == 360°).

members.name: skewX
members.documentation: Horizontal shear, in radians.

members.name: skewY
members.documentation: Vertical shear, in radians.

members.name: rotateX
members.documentation:
Rotation around the X axis (a flip toward/away from the viewer) in
turns, drawn with perspective. Identity is `0.0`.

members.name: rotateY
members.documentation:
Rotation around the Y axis (a turn like a door or card flip) in turns,
drawn with perspective. Identity is `0.0`.

members.name: blur
members.documentation:
Gaussian blur applied to the whole widget, as a sigma in logical
pixels. Identity is `0.0` (no blur, no extra compositing layer).

members.name: tint
members.documentation:
A colour laid over the widget's painted pixels (blended with
`BlendMode.srcATop`, so transparent areas stay transparent). Use an
alpha below `0xFF` for a wash. `null` means no tint.

members.name: opacity
members.documentation:
Opacity from `0.0` (fully transparent) to `1.0` (fully opaque,
identity).

members.name: color
members.documentation: Background color painted behind the child. `null` means transparent.

members.name: borderRadius
members.documentation: Clip radius applied to the widget and its [color]/[boxShadow].

members.name: boxShadow
members.documentation: Shadows painted behind the widget.

members.name: identity
members.documentation:
The identity animation: every transform/opacity property at the value
that produces no visual change, with no color, border radius, or
shadow.

members.name: lerp
members.documentation:
Interpolates between this animation and [other] at position [t]
(`0.0` = this, `1.0` = [other]).

For each scalar property: if both sides are `null` the result is
`null`; if only one side is set, the other side falls back to its
[identity] value before interpolating. [color], [borderRadius], and
[boxShadow] are interpolated with `Color.lerp`, `BorderRadius.lerp`,
and `BoxShadow.lerpList`, which already handle `null` correctly.

members.name: copyWith
members.signature:
NibAnim copyWith({
    double? x,
    double? y,
    double? scale,
    double? scaleX,
    double? scaleY,
    double? rotate,
    double? skewX,
    double? skewY,
    double? rotateX,
    double? rotateY,
    double? blur,
    Color? tint,
    double? opacity,
    Color? color,
    BorderRadius? borderRadius,
    List<BoxShadow>? boxShadow,
  })
members.documentation:
Returns a copy of this animation with the given properties replaced.

Properties left as `null` keep their current value.

members.name: merge
members.documentation:
Returns a copy of this animation with every non-null property of
[other] overriding the corresponding property of this animation.

Used by the Variants system to cascade a child's variant state over
its parent's.

motion.name: NibAnimPresets
motion.documentation:
A library of common, ready-to-use animations for `NibMotion`.

The [List<NibKeyframe>] presets are passed to `NibMotion.keyframes` (e.g.
`NibMotion(keyframes: NibAnimPresets.shake, child: ...)`) to play a
multi-step animation. The [NibAnim] presets are single-state snapshots
meant for `NibMotion.initial`/`NibMotion.animate` (e.g.
`NibMotion(initial: NibAnimPresets.fadeUp, animate: NibAnim(opacity: 1, y: 0))`).

members.name: shake
members.documentation:
Rapid left-right oscillation, commonly used for input validation
feedback (see `NibShake`).

members.name: bounceIn
members.documentation:
Drops in from above and settles with a small bounce, commonly used for
enter animations (see `NibBounce`).

members.name: pulse
members.documentation:
Scales up and back down, commonly used as a repeating "heartbeat"
animation (see `NibPulse`).

members.name: rubberBand
members.documentation:
Overshoots non-uniformly on each axis and settles, like a rubber band
snapping back into shape (see `NibRubberBand`).

members.name: wiggle
members.documentation: Gentle rotation oscillation.

members.name: fadeUp
members.documentation: Fade in from below — a common enter animation starting state.

members.name: fadeDown
members.documentation: Fade in from above.

members.name: fadeLeft
members.documentation: Fade in from the left.

members.name: fadeRight
members.documentation: Fade in from the right.

members.name: zoomIn
members.documentation: Zoom in from slightly smaller than identity.

members.name: zoomOut
members.documentation: Zoom out from slightly larger than identity.

motion.name: NibAnimationSequence
motion.documentation:
A fluent builder for a sequence of animation steps driven against a
single [NibMotionController].

Chain `.animate()`, `.wait()`, and `.call()` to record steps, optionally
`.loop()` to repeat them, then call `.play()` to start execution:

```dart
await NibAnimationSequence(controller)
  .animate(const NibAnim(y: -20, opacity: 0))
  .wait(const Duration(milliseconds: 100))
  .animate(const NibAnim(y: 0, opacity: 1), transition: NibTransition.springGentle)
  .play();
```

Internally, each step is executed in order via `async`/`await` against
[controller] — `.animate()` steps delegate to
[NibMotionController.start], so the same per-step animate/wait semantics
as [NibMotionController.sequence] apply, but `.call()` callbacks and
`.loop()` repetition are layered on top without modifying
[NibMotionController] itself.

members.name: NibAnimationSequence
members.documentation:
Creates a sequence builder over [controller]. Call `.animate()`,
`.wait()`, `.call()`, and `.loop()` to record steps, then `.play()` to
run them.

members.name: controller
members.documentation: The controller this sequence drives.

members.name: animate
members.documentation:
Queues an animation step that animates [controller] toward [target]
using [transition] (or each attached `NibMotion`'s default transition
if `null`).

members.name: wait
members.documentation: Queues a delay of [duration] before the next step starts.

members.name: call
members.documentation:
Queues a synchronous [callback] to run inline, at this point in the
sequence.

members.name: loop
members.signature:
NibAnimationSequence loop(
      [int? times, NibLoopMode mode = NibLoopMode.restart])
members.documentation:
Repeats every step recorded so far, either [times] times, or forever
if [times] is omitted/`null`.

Must be called at most once, after recording the steps to repeat and
before calling [play].

members.name: play
members.documentation:
Starts executing the recorded steps in order.

If [loop] was called with a finite count, the steps repeat that many
times and the returned [Future] completes once the final repetition
finishes. If [loop] was called with no argument (forever), the steps
repeat indefinitely and the returned [Future] **never completes** —
call [stop] to halt playback (the future remains incomplete even
then; it exists only to let finite sequences be awaited).

Calling [play] again while already playing has no additional effect
beyond returning a new future tracking the (still in-progress) run.

members.name: stop
members.documentation:
Cancels an in-progress or looping sequence. Steps already started will
still finish their current `run` (e.g. an in-flight animation or
wait), but no further steps will execute.

members.name: dispose
members.documentation:
Stops playback and releases this sequence's recorded steps. The
underlying [controller] is not disposed — callers own its lifecycle.

motion.name: NibBounce
motion.documentation:
Plays a "drop in from above and bounce" entrance animation on [child]
using [NibAnimPresets.bounceIn].

```dart
NibBounce(
  child: const Text('Welcome!'),
)
```

members.name: NibBounce
members.signature:
const NibBounce(
      {super.key,
      required this.child,
      this.duration = const Duration(milliseconds: 800)})
members.documentation: Creates a `NibBounce`.

members.name: child
members.documentation: The widget to animate in.

members.name: duration
members.documentation: How long the bounce-in entrance takes to play out.

motion.name: NibBubbleEmitter
motion.documentation:
Deterministic, bounded decorative air-bubble motion for one water controller.

Rise and lateral drift are artistic approximations, not fluid simulation.
The controller owns advancement. Do not share an emitter between controllers.

members.name: NibBubbleEmitter
members.signature:
NibBubbleEmitter(
      {this.seed = 1,
      this.maxBubbles = 6,
      this.interval = .55,
      this.minRadius = 11,
      this.maxRadius = 24,
      this.minLifetime = 4.5,
      this.maxLifetime = 6.7,
      this.drift = 25})
members.documentation: Creates at most ten bubbles; defaults match a quiet, slow rise.

members.name: seed
members.documentation: Seed reused by reset for replay.

members.name: maxBubbles
members.documentation: Maximum live bodies, within the shader's ten-body capacity.

members.name: interval
members.documentation: Seconds between emission attempts.

members.name: minRadius
members.documentation: Minimum radius in logical pixels.

members.name: maxRadius
members.documentation: Maximum radius before the small exit expansion.

members.name: minLifetime
members.documentation: Shortest rise lifetime in seconds.

members.name: maxLifetime
members.documentation: Longest rise lifetime in seconds.

members.name: drift
members.documentation: Maximum lateral drift in logical pixels.

members.name: emitting
members.documentation: Whether new bubbles may be emitted.

members.name: isActive
members.documentation: Whether emission or existing bodies still need a frame clock.

members.name: stop
members.documentation: Stops spawning while existing bubbles finish their rise.

members.name: start
members.documentation: Allows spawning again. Notify the owning controller via setEmitting.

members.name: reset
members.documentation: Clears bodies and resets the seeded sequence, preserving emission policy.

members.name: advance
members.documentation:
Advances bounded active time and returns one batched scene snapshot.
The owning controller supplies at most 66 ms per frame.

motion.name: NibDissolve
motion.documentation:
Dissolves [child] in or out using a noise-pattern fragment shader,
instead of a uniform opacity fade.

A drop-in replacement for [FadeTransition] in page/element transitions
that want a more textured, GPU-driven look. The dissolve progress is
driven by a raw [Ticker] writing into a [MotionValue<double>] — the same
pattern [SpringSolver] and `NibShimmer` use — so the running animation
never causes a widget rebuild.

If the bundled dissolve shader hasn't finished compiling (or fails to
compile in this environment), [child] is painted with a plain opacity
fade as a fallback so the transition still reads correctly.

members.name: NibDissolve
members.signature:
const NibDissolve({
    super.key,
    required this.child,
    this.duration = const Duration(milliseconds: 500),
    this.direction = NibDissolveDirection.outward,
    this.noiseScale = 0.02,
    this.onComplete,
  })
members.documentation: Creates a dissolve transition around [child].

members.name: child
members.documentation: The widget being dissolved in or out.

members.name: duration
members.documentation: How long the dissolve animation takes.

members.name: direction
members.documentation:
Whether the dissolve animates from invisible to visible
([NibDissolveDirection.inward]) or visible to invisible
([NibDissolveDirection.outward]).

members.name: noiseScale
members.documentation:
The grain size of the dissolve noise pattern. Smaller values produce
finer grain.

members.name: onComplete
members.documentation: Called once the dissolve animation finishes.

motion.name: NibDissolveDirection
motion.documentation: Which direction a [NibDissolve] animation runs.

members.name: inward
members.documentation: Animates from fully dissolved to fully visible.

members.name: outward
members.documentation: Animates from fully visible to fully dissolved.

motion.name: NibDragConfig
motion.documentation:
Configuration for `NibMotion.drag`.

If `NibMotion.drag` is `null`, dragging is disabled entirely.

members.name: NibDragConfig
members.signature:
const NibDragConfig({
    this.axis,
    this.constraints,
    this.elastic = false,
    this.elasticFactor = 0.2,
    this.onDragStart,
    this.onDragEnd,
    this.releaseMode = NibDragReleaseMode.springBack,
    this.snapPoints,
    this.snapProjection = Duration.zero,
  })
members.documentation: Creates a drag configuration.

members.name: axis
members.documentation: Locks dragging to a single axis. `null` allows free dragging.

members.name: constraints
members.documentation:
The bounding box the drag offset is confined to, as offsets *from the
resting position* (e.g. `Rect.fromLTRB(-120, 0, 120, 0)` allows 120px
either way), not absolute coordinates. Relative to the
position the widget was at before the drag started. `null` means
unconstrained.

members.name: elastic
members.documentation:
Whether dragging past [constraints] applies rubber-band resistance
instead of clamping outright.

members.name: elasticFactor
members.documentation:
How much of the drag past [constraints] is applied when [elastic] is
`true`. Expected range `0.1`-`0.5`; smaller values are stiffer.

members.name: onDragStart
members.documentation: Called when a drag gesture begins.

members.name: onDragEnd
members.documentation:
Called when a drag gesture ends, with velocity in receiver-local
pixels per second (the same units as the drag offset).

members.name: releaseMode
members.documentation:
How the widget settles once the drag gesture ends. Ignored if
[snapPoints] is set and non-empty.

members.name: snapPoints
members.documentation:
Points are offsets from the resting position (not absolute coordinates).

If set and non-empty, the widget springs to the nearest of these points
on release instead of following [releaseMode].

members.name: snapProjection
members.documentation:
How far ahead, along the release velocity, to look when choosing the
nearest of [snapPoints]. With the default [Duration.zero] the snap point
nearest the release *position* wins; a value such as
`Duration(milliseconds: 150)` lets a quick flick reach the next point.

motion.name: NibDragReleaseMode
motion.documentation: How a draggable `NibMotion` settles once the drag gesture ends.

members.name: springBack
members.documentation: Spring back to the position the widget was at before the drag started.

members.name: inertia
members.documentation: Coast to a natural stop using the release velocity.

members.name: stay
members.documentation: Stay exactly where the drag left it.

motion.name: NibDraggable
motion.documentation:
A higher-level drag widget with boundaries, axis locking, and snap-back.

Unlike `NibMotion.drag` (which integrates dragging into the full
animation system), `NibDraggable` is a focused, standalone widget for the
common case of "let the user drag this around, optionally constrained to
[bounds] or a single [axis], and spring it back to [snapTarget] (or its
origin) on release."

translation, written directly from `GestureDetector.onPanUpdate` and read
directly by a [RenderProxyBox] during `paint` — dragging never triggers a
widget rebuild.

motion.documentation:
Animates the drawing of [path] — like a signature or SVG stroke
animation.

`NibDrawPath` drives a `MotionValue<double>` progress value (`0.0` to
`1.0`) with a Ticker-based tween over [duration]/[curve] — the same
per-frame-write-into-a-MotionValue pattern [SpringSolver] uses, just
curve-tweened instead of spring-simulated. The underlying `RenderBox`
reads [path]'s `PathMetrics` directly in `paint()`, calling
`extractPath(0, length * progress)` to draw only the revealed portion —
animating never triggers a widget rebuild.

motion.name: NibFlip
motion.documentation:
A 3D card-flip widget that reveals [back] in place of [front] (or vice
versa) when [isFlipped] changes.

```dart
bool _isFlipped = false;

NibFlip(
  isFlipped: _isFlipped,
  front: const Card(child: Text('Question')),
  back: const Card(child: Text('Answer')),
)

// Elsewhere, e.g. on tap:
setState(() => _isFlipped = !_isFlipped);
```

The flip progress is driven by a raw [Ticker] writing to a
[MotionValue<double>] that a custom [RenderObject] reads directly during
paint — consistent with the rest of this package, no
[AnimationController] is used as the driver for this non-`NibMotion`
property. At progress `>= 0.5` the visible face switches from [front] to
[back] (or back again).

vertical (Y) axis, [Axis.vertical] rotates around the horizontal (X)
axis.

motion.name: NibGlass
motion.documentation:
A "liquid glass" surface: a physically-modelled glass dome over the
backdrop — Apple's Liquid Glass material, rendered with the bundled
`liquid_glass.frag` backdrop shader. The glass is [thickness] px deep with
a quarter-circle dome profile: optically flat in the center (the backdrop
stays sharp and straight) and curving to horizontal at the rim, where real
Snell's-law refraction (driven by [refractiveIndex]) bends the backdrop
strongly inward. [chromaticAberration] adds red/blue dispersion at the
rim, [saturation] makes the backdrop's colors pop through the glass, and a
rim highlight derived from the background color tracks [lightDirection].

True edge refraction requires the **Impeller** rendering backend
([ui.ImageFilter.isShaderFilterSupported]). On any other backend — or before
the shader has compiled, or when laid out without a bounded size — `NibGlass`
falls back to a frosted blur + tint + painted rim highlight, which still reads
as glass but without the lensing. It never throws.

`NibGlass` is a low-level engine widget: it takes a fully-resolved
[tint]/[lightDirection]/etc. `nib_components`' `NibLiquidGlass` wraps it with
theme tokens, gesture-driven light, and the animation contract.

members.signature:
const NibGlass({
    super.key,
    required this.child,
    this.borderRadius = const BorderRadius.all(Radius.circular(24)),
    this.clipper,
    this.blurSigma = 1,
    this.tint = const Color(0x14FFFFFF),
    this.thickness = 20,
    this.refractiveIndex = 1.2,
    this.chromaticAberration = 0.03,
    this.saturation = 1.3,
    this.highlight = 0.5,
    this.lightDirection = const Offset(-0.5, -1),
  })

Creates a liquid-glass surface painting [child] over a refracted,
subtly tinted backdrop.

members.name: child
members.documentation: The content painted on top of the glass.

members.name: borderRadius
members.documentation: Corner radius of the glass surface (ignored when [clipper] is set).

members.name: clipper
members.documentation:
Custom shape for the glass. When non-null it clips the surface (capsule,
blob, arbitrary path) instead of [borderRadius].

members.name: blurSigma
members.documentation:
Gaussian blur applied to the backdrop. Kept near zero by default — liquid
glass is clear, not frosted; the edge refraction carries the effect.

members.name: tint
members.documentation:
Tint painted over the backdrop; the alpha channel is the mix amount.
Subtle by default — the glass is mostly clear.

members.name: thickness
members.documentation:
Depth of the glass dome, in logical pixels. The surface is flat deeper
than [thickness] px inside the shape and curves down to the rim over
that band — thicker glass refracts a wider, stronger band. Only used on
the shader path.

members.name: refractiveIndex
members.documentation:
Index of refraction of the glass. 1.0 means no bending; Apple-style
liquid glass sits around 1.2. Only used on the shader path.

members.name: chromaticAberration
members.documentation:
Chromatic aberration (dispersion) strength: how far the red and blue
channels' refractions separate at the rim. 0 disables the extra texture
taps. Only used on the shader path.

members.name: saturation
members.documentation:
Saturation boost applied to the backdrop seen through the glass —
1.0 leaves it unchanged, >1 makes colors pop. Only used on the shader
path.

members.name: highlight
members.documentation: Rim-highlight (edge lighting) intensity, 0..1.

members.name: lightDirection
members.documentation: Direction the specular highlight comes from (points toward the light).

members.name: debugShaderPathAvailable
members.documentation:
Diagnostic: whether the real shader path can actually run on this device —
i.e. the bundled `liquid_glass.frag` program compiles AND
`ImageFilter.shader` is supported (Impeller). Returns `false` when the
glass would fall back to a plain blur (shader asset not bundled, or a
non-Impeller backend). Intended for debugging/diagnostics, not layout.

masking the gradient onto the text's painted pixels via `BlendMode.srcIn`.

The sweep position is driven by a single `MotionValue<double>` (`_offset`)
that a `Ticker` owned by `_NibGradientTextState` advances every frame —
mirroring how `SpringSolver`/`InertiaSolver` tick a `Ticker` and write into
a `MotionValue` rather than calling `setState`. `RenderNibGradientText`
listens to that `MotionValue` and repaints via `markNeedsPaint()`, so the
sweep animates without ever rebuilding the widget tree.

immediately instead of only on the next navigation.

`WidgetsBinding.reassembleApplication`) and fires the ambient
`NibMotionReplaySignal`. In release/profile builds it does nothing and
adds only the replay scope.

One point in a multi-step animation driven by `NibMotion.keyframes`.

`1.0`) along the animation, with an optional per-segment [curve].

previous keyframe's [value] to this one.

a [NibSpringCurve] (unit step response stretched over the segment). An
underdamped spring overshoots this keyframe's value and settles on it at
the segment's end. Mutually exclusive with [curve].

motion.name: NibLayout
motion.documentation:
Which changes of its own layout a `NibMotion` animates.

Set through `NibMotion.layout`. The widget is measured in the coordinate
space of the nearest `NibLayoutScope` (or the whole box-model subtree above
it, bounded by the nearest scrollable), so scrolling never counts as a
layout change.

members.name: none
members.documentation:
Layout changes are not animated, even when an enclosing
`NibLayoutDefaults` asks for them.

members.name: position
members.documentation: Animate position changes (FLIP translation).

members.name: size
members.documentation:
Animate size changes (FLIP scale about the widget's centre, with the
position held). The child is scaled, not re-laid out, so text and images
stretch for the duration of the animation.

members.name: both
members.documentation: Animate both position and size changes.

members.name: inherit
members.documentation:
Use the enclosing `NibLayoutDefaults` layout, or [none] when there is
none (default). Being distinct from an explicit [none] lets a child opt
out of an inherited default.

motion.name: NibLayoutChannelMode
motion.documentation: Where a layout FLIP's position offset is stored.

members.name: channels
members.documentation:
In dedicated layout channels, painted on top of the widget's own
transform. The default: a widget can animate `x`/`y` and FLIP at once.

members.name: translate
members.documentation:
Directly in the widget's own `translateX`/`translateY` values. Used by
`NibLayoutGroup`, whose children are laid out and moved only by layout, so
the FLIP is observable as the widget's translation. The widget must not
animate its own `x`/`y` in this mode (the FLIP owns them and rests at 0).

motion.name: NibLayoutDefaults
motion.documentation:
Supplies a default [NibLayout] to descendant `NibMotion`s that leave their
own `layout` at [NibLayout.none].

This is what lets `NibPresence.layout` turn on FLIP reflow for every child
with one call. A `NibMotion` that sets `layout` explicitly (anything other
than [NibLayout.none]) keeps its own value; because [NibLayout.none] is the
constructor default it cannot opt out — wrap it in
`NibLayoutDefaults(layout: NibLayout.none, …)` instead.

The value is read when a `NibMotion` is created and on each rebuild; it
does not subscribe, so changing it does not rebuild descendants.

members.name: NibLayoutDefaults
members.documentation: Creates a scope applying [layout] to descendants.

members.name: layout
members.documentation: The layout mode applied to descendants that do not set their own.

members.name: maybeOf
members.documentation: The nearest enclosing [NibLayoutDefaults], or `null`.

motion.name: NibLayoutGroup
motion.documentation:
Animates [children] to their new positions whenever a rebuild changes
their layout, using the FLIP (First, Last, Invert, Play) technique.

Each widget in [children] must carry a non-null, unique [Key], which
identifies it across rebuilds so [NibLayoutGroup] can measure how far it
moved:

- **First:** before the new layout is applied, the current position of
  every child present in both the old and new [children] is recorded.
- **Last:** after the new layout is applied (via
  [WidgetsBinding.addPostFrameCallback]), each tracked child's new
  position is compared against its recorded one.
- **Invert:** if a child moved, its [NibMotion] is immediately offset
  (no animation) so it visually stays at its old position.
- **Play:** that offset is animated back to zero with [transition],
  so the child appears to travel smoothly from its old position to its
  new one.

Each child is a `NibMotion(layout: NibLayout.position)` in
[NibLayoutChannelMode.translate] mode inside a [NibLayoutScope], so the
group is a thin `Column` over the same per-widget mechanism you get from
`NibMotion(layout:)` anywhere else; the FLIP is observable as each child's
own translation.

A child whose key is newly added to [children] mounts without a FLIP
animation. A child whose key is removed from [children] stops being
tracked; re-adding it later is treated as a new child.

The widgets to lay out and track. Each must carry a non-null, unique

members.documentation:
The transition used to animate a moved child back to its new position.

Defaults to [NibTransition.springGentle].

members.documentation: Called (after the frame) for each child added after the first build.

members.name: onChildExit
members.documentation:
Called (after the frame) for each child removed from [children]; a group
child has no exit animation, it leaves at once.

members.name: onChildMove
members.documentation: Called when a FLIP starts for a child that moved.

members.name: onAnimationStart
members.documentation: Called when the first FLIP of a batch starts.

members.name: onAnimationComplete

Called when every FLIP started since [onAnimationStart] has finished (or
was superseded by a newer one for the same child).

motion.name: NibLayoutScope
motion.documentation:
Defines the coordinate space `NibMotion.layout` widgets are measured in,
and connects `layoutId`s across the subtree.

Wrap the container whose children animate (a `Wrap`, a `Stack`, a whole
screen). Movement of the scope itself — the container being resized,
re-positioned, or scrolled — is *not* a layout change for its descendants;
only movement relative to the scope is. Without a scope, widgets are
measured up to the nearest scrollable, so a moving container above them
animates its children too.

A scope is also required for `NibMotion.layoutId`: a widget that mounts with
an id another (just-unmounted) widget in the same scope was using animates
from that widget's last rectangle — a shared-element transition that works
across parents.

members.name: NibLayoutScope
members.documentation: Creates a layout scope around [child].

members.name: child
members.documentation: The subtree measured in this scope's coordinate space.

members.name: maybeOf
members.documentation: The nearest scope's shared-id registry, or null.

motion.name: NibLayoutSizeMode
motion.documentation: How a size change of a `NibMotion(layout: size | both)` is played.

members.name: scale
members.documentation:
FLIP scale about the centre (default): cheap, but the child (text,
images) stretches for the duration of the animation.

members.name: clip
members.documentation:
The child is laid out at its *final* size and revealed through an
interpolated clip anchored at its top-left: nothing is stretched. A
shrinking widget simply shows its new (smaller) content at once, since
the old pixels no longer exist — combine with a sibling `position` FLIP
for the surrounding reflow.

motion.name: NibLoopMode
motion.documentation: How a looping [NibAnimationSequence] repeats.

members.name: restart
members.documentation: Every repetition replays the steps from the first one.

members.name: pingPong
members.documentation:
Alternates direction: forward passes replay the steps in order; backward
passes replay them in reverse, animating back through the earlier
animate targets until the first target is reached again. `call` and
`wait` steps run in both directions.

members.name: seamless
members.documentation:
Like [restart], but when the first animate step targets exactly the
state the last animate step ended on, that step is skipped on repeats so
there is no dead time at the seam.

motion.name: NibModalRoute
motion.documentation:
A modal route (dialog, sheet, popover) whose content enters and exits with
[NibMotion] physics.

Built on [PopupRoute], so it gets a barrier, back-button/`Navigator.pop`
dismissal and result returning for free. Widgets-only: no Material
dependency.

```dart
final ok = await Navigator.of(context).push(NibModalRoute<bool>(
  builder: (context) => MyDialog(),
));
```

The content is [initial] when the route starts, springs to [animate] on
enter, and to [exit] when popped. A pop during the enter animation reverses
it from the current position *and velocity*.

`NibMotion` owns a [MotionValue] for each animatable property and drives
them with [SpringSolver] (when [NibTransition.spring] is set) or a
curve-based tween (otherwise). The [MotionValue]s are passed straight to
[RenderNibMotion], so animating never triggers a widget rebuild.

The animation values applied immediately on first build, before any
transition runs. Defaults to [NibAnim.identity].

Either a [NibAnim] or a [String] naming an entry in [variants].

Read **once**, when the widget's state is created: changing it on a
later rebuild has no effect. Give the widget a new `Key` to restart from
a different `initial`, or change [animate] to move an existing widget.

members.name: animate
members.documentation:
The animation values to transition toward. `null` means "no change",
unless [variants] is set and an ancestor `NibMotion` has propagated a
variant name that matches one of its keys.

Either a [NibAnim] or a [String] naming an entry in [variants]. When a
[String], the name is also propagated to descendant `NibMotion`s with a
matching [variants] entry and no explicit [animate].

members.name: exit
members.documentation:
The animation values to transition toward when an ancestor
`NibPresence` removes this widget. Requires [key] to be set.

members.name: whileTap
members.documentation: The animation values to transition toward while this widget is pressed.

members.name: whileHover
members.documentation:
The animation values to transition toward while the pointer hovers over
this widget.

members.name: whileFocus
members.documentation:
The animation values to transition toward while this widget has input
focus.

members.name: whileDrag
members.documentation:
The animation values to transition toward while this widget is being
dragged. Reverted to [animate] (or [initial]) when the drag ends.

members.name: drag
members.documentation: Enables dragging this widget. If `null`, dragging is disabled.

members.name: whileInView
members.documentation:
The animation values to transition toward while this widget is visible
within the screen, according to [viewport].

Unless [viewport]'s `once` is `true`, this reverts to [animate] (or
[initial]) when the widget scrolls out of view.

members.name: viewport
members.documentation:
Configures the visibility check used by [whileInView]. Defaults to
[NibInViewConfig.new]'s defaults when [whileInView] is set.

members.name: variants
members.documentation:
Named animation states this widget can resolve [initial]/[animate]
string names against, and that it checks against the variant name
propagated by an ancestor `NibMotion` when [animate] is `null`.

members.name: keyframes
members.documentation:
A multi-step enter animation that overrides [initial] and [animate].

When non-null, this widget starts at `keyframes.first.value`, then runs
a single tween [AnimationController] from `0.0` to `1.0` over
[NibTransition.duration], applying [computeAnimFromKeyframes] at each
tick. Spring transitions ([NibTransition.spring]) are not supported with
[keyframes]; [NibTransition.curve] is used as the default per-segment
curve.

members.name: motionValues
members.documentation:
Pre-built [MotionValue]s that drive this widget's animatable
properties directly, bypassing the internal spring/tween system for
any property they provide.

members.name: transition
members.documentation:
The transition used for [animate] (and as a default for gesture
states that don't specify their own).

If `null`, falls back to `NibMotionConfig.defaultTransitionOf(context)`
(or [NibTransition]'s defaults if there is no `NibMotionConfig`
ancestor).

members.name: spring
members.documentation:
Shorthand for `transition: NibTransition.of(spring)`: a spring-driven
transition using this description (for example a [NibSpring] token).
Mutually exclusive with [transition].

members.name: controller
members.documentation: An optional external handle for driving this widget's animations.

members.name: repeatAnimationInLoop
members.documentation:
When `true`, instead of running the normal one-shot entrance animation
(`initial` -> `animate`, or [keyframes] `0.0` -> `1.0`), this widget
ping-pongs forever: `initial` -> `animate` (or [keyframes] `0.0` ->
`1.0` -> `0.0` -> `1.0` ...) -> `initial` -> `animate` -> ..., using
[NibTransition.duration]/[NibTransition.curve] from [transition] (or
`NibMotionConfig.defaultTransitionOf(context)`).

Has no effect if [motionValues] is set. If
`NibMotionConfig.shouldReduceMotion(context)` is `true`, this jumps to
the end of the cycle once and does not loop.

Can be toggled at runtime via [NibMotionController.repeat] (using
[controller]), independent of this field's value.

members.name: loopMode
members.documentation:
How [repeatAnimationInLoop] repeats: [NibLoopMode.pingPong] (default)
plays `initial → animate → initial …`; [NibLoopMode.restart] (and
[NibLoopMode.seamless], which is identical here) jumps back to `initial`
each cycle — use it when the end state visually matches the start.

members.name: loopPhase
members.documentation:
Starting progress of a repeating animation, in the range `[0, 1)`.

Offsets ambient loops without delaying their first visible frame.
Ping-pong loops start on their forward leg. Ignored for one-shot motion.

members.name: reverseTransition
members.documentation:
The transition used when this widget *returns* from a temporary state:
releasing [whileTap]/[whileHover]/[whileFocus]/[whileDrag] or leaving
[whileInView]. Lets the way back differ from the way in (e.g. a slow
press, a snappy release). Falls back to [transition].

members.name: exitTransition
members.documentation:
The transition used by the [exit] animation when a `NibPresence` removes
this widget. Falls back to [transition].

members.name: layout
members.documentation:
Which of this widget's own layout changes to animate.

Whenever a rebuild (a reorder, a `Positioned` move, a size change…)
moves or resizes this widget relative to its `NibLayoutScope`, it is
visually kept where it was and animated to its new place with
[layoutTransition] — FLIP, in any parent (`Column`, `Row`, `Wrap`,
`Stack`, grids). The animation runs on paint-time transforms: it never
rebuilds the child, continues from the painted position and velocity if
interrupted, and jumps under reduced motion. See `doc/layout.md`.

members.name: layoutSizeMode
members.documentation:
How size changes ([NibLayout.size]/[NibLayout.both]) are played:
[NibLayoutSizeMode.scale] stretches the child, [NibLayoutSizeMode.clip]
lays it out at its final size and reveals it through a growing clip.

members.name: layoutChannelMode
members.documentation:
Where the position part of a layout FLIP is kept: in dedicated channels
([NibLayoutChannelMode.channels], default) or directly in this widget's
`translateX`/`translateY` ([NibLayoutChannelMode.translate], what
`NibLayoutGroup` uses). In translate mode this widget must not animate its
own `x`/`y`: the FLIP owns them and they rest at 0.

members.name: layoutId
members.documentation:
Identity for shared-layout transitions: when a widget with this id
mounts in the same `NibLayoutScope` right after another one with the same
id unmounted, it animates from the old widget's rectangle. Requires
[layout] other than [NibLayout.none] and an enclosing `NibLayoutScope`.

members.name: layoutTransition
members.documentation:
How a layout change is animated back to rest. Defaults to
[NibTransition.springGentle]; only `spring`, `duration` and `curve` are
used.

members.name: onLayoutAnimationStart
members.documentation: Called when a layout animation starts.

members.name: onLayoutAnimationComplete
members.documentation:
Called when the latest layout animation has settled (not when it was
superseded by a newer one).

members.name: child
members.documentation: The widget below this one in the tree.

motion.name: NibMotionConfig
motion.documentation:
Global configuration for `NibMotion` widgets.

Provide a `NibMotionConfig` as an ancestor to override the system's
reduced-motion preference and/or set a default [NibTransition] for
`NibMotion` widgets that don't specify their own.

```dart
NibMotionConfig(
  defaultTransition: NibTransition.springGentle,
  child: MyApp(),
)
```

members.name: NibMotionConfig
members.signature:
const NibMotionConfig({
    super.key,
    this.reducedMotion,
    this.defaultTransition = const NibTransition(),
    this.entranceWarmup = const Duration(milliseconds: 400),
    required super.child,
  })
members.documentation:
Creates a `NibMotionConfig`.

If [reducedMotion] is `null`, `NibMotion` falls back to
`MediaQuery.of(context).disableAnimations`.

members.name: reducedMotion
members.documentation: Overrides `MediaQuery.disableAnimations` when non-`null`.

members.name: defaultTransition
members.documentation:
The transition used by `NibMotion` widgets that don't specify their own
[NibMotion.transition].

members.name: entranceWarmup
members.documentation:
How long after the app starts `NibMotion` entrance animations
(`animate`/`keyframes` on first build, and an immediately-visible
`whileInView`) should wait before starting.

This absorbs the brief delay on real devices between Flutter rendering
its first frame and the native splash screen actually disappearing, so
entrance animations don't run unseen underneath it. Widgets created
after this warm-up window has elapsed (e.g. on a later screen) start
immediately, as before.

Defaults to 400ms, which comfortably covers the gap between Flutter's
first frame and the platform's native splash screen actually
disappearing on a real device — so entrance animations don't run (and
finish) unseen underneath it. See also [NibMotionGate] for apps that
preserve a native splash screen for longer than this.

members.name: resetAppStartTime
members.documentation:
Resets the app-start timestamp used by [remainingWarmup] to now.

Intended for tests.

members.name: setReducedMotion
members.documentation:
Globally forces (`true`), disables (`false`), or clears (`null`) the
reduced-motion override, regardless of any [NibMotionConfig] ancestor or
`MediaQuery` setting.

Intended for tests; production code should prefer the [reducedMotion]
constructor parameter.

members.name: maybeOf
members.documentation:
Returns the nearest ancestor `NibMotionConfig`, or `null` if there is
none.

members.name: shouldReduceMotion
members.documentation:
Resolves whether `NibMotion` animations should jump straight to their
target instead of animating.

Resolution order: [setReducedMotion] override, then
[NibMotionConfig.reducedMotion], then
`MediaQuery.of(context).disableAnimations`.

members.name: watchReducedMotion
members.documentation:
Like [shouldReduceMotion], but registers a dependency on the nearest
[NibMotionConfig] and `MediaQuery`, so the calling element rebuilds
(and `didChangeDependencies` runs) when the preference changes.

members.name: defaultTransitionOf
members.documentation:
Resolves the default transition for `NibMotion` widgets that don't
specify their own [NibMotion.transition].

members.name: remainingWarmup
members.documentation:
Returns how much longer entrance animations should wait before
starting, based on [entranceWarmup] and how long ago the app started.

Returns [Duration.zero] once the warm-up window has elapsed.

members.name: globalDefaultTransition
members.documentation:
The process-wide default [NibTransition] set by the most recent
[init] call.

This is distinct from the per-subtree [defaultTransition] resolved by
[defaultTransitionOf] — code that runs outside a `BuildContext` (e.g.
imperative animation setup) can read this directly.

members.name: reducedMotionEnabled
members.documentation:
The process-wide reduced-motion preference set by the most recent
[init] call's `respectReducedMotion` resolution.

This reflects [init]'s one-time startup resolution; it does not track
later `MediaQuery` or [setReducedMotion] changes — prefer
[shouldReduceMotion] inside a `BuildContext` for that.

members.name: init
members.documentation:
Call once at app startup, before `runApp()`, to pre-load
`nib_motion`'s bundled fragment shaders and configure framework-wide
defaults.

When [preloadShaders] is `true` (the default), this kicks off
compilation of every shader bundled with `nib_motion` (see
[NibShaderLoader.preloadAll]) so the first `NibShimmer`/`NibDissolve`
built doesn't pay that cost on its own first frame. Shader preload
failures (e.g. the host app hasn't declared `nib_motion`'s shader
assets) are swallowed — affected widgets fall back to painting their
child without the shader effect.

[defaultTransition] becomes the process-wide [globalDefaultTransition].
When [respectReducedMotion] is `true` (the default), [init] also reads
`WidgetsBinding.instance.platformDispatcher.accessibilityFeatures`'s
reduce-motion preference once at startup and stores it in
[reducedMotionEnabled]; when `false`, [reducedMotionEnabled] is left as
`false` regardless of the platform setting.

```dart
void main() async {
  WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized();
  await NibMotionConfig.init();
  runApp(MyApp());
}
```

motion.name: NibMotionController

members.name: attach
members.documentation:
Attaches this controller to [animator]. Called by `_NibMotionState`
during `initState`/`didUpdateWidget`.

members.name: detach
members.documentation:
Detaches [animator] from this controller. Called by `_NibMotionState`
during `dispose`/`didUpdateWidget`.

members.name: start
members.signature:
Future<void> start(
      {NibAnim? target,
      List<NibKeyframe>? keyframes,
      NibTransition? transition})
members.documentation:
Drives every attached `NibMotion`:
- `start(target: ..., transition: ...)` — animates toward `target` (old behavior).
- `start(keyframes: [...], transition: ...)` — plays that keyframe sequence once.
- `start()` (both null) — replays each widget's entrance animation
  (`initial` -> `animate`/`keyframes`, or restarts its
  `repeatAnimationInLoop` loop).

Only one of `target`/`keyframes` may be provided.

members.name: motionValueOf
members.documentation:
The live [MotionValue] behind [property] of the first attached
`NibMotion`, or `null` if none is attached yet.

It is the widget's own value, so it carries `value` and `velocity` and
can be listened to (`addListener`) without rebuilding anything.

members.name: velocityOf
members.documentation:
The current velocity of [property] in units per second (`0` when
nothing is attached or the property is at rest).

members.name: velocities
members.documentation: A snapshot of the velocity of every [NibProperty].

members.name: initialAnim
members.documentation:
The start state of the first attached `NibMotion` (its `initial`),
merged over [NibAnim.identity]; [NibAnim.identity] if none is attached.

members.name: set
members.documentation:
Immediately sets every attached `NibMotion` to [target], with no
animation.

Each property's velocity is reset to zero unless [keepVelocity] is true,
in which case a following [start] continues the motion in progress.

members.name: stop
members.documentation:
Stops all in-progress animations on every attached `NibMotion`,
freezing each animated property at its current value.

members.name: repeat
members.documentation:
Enables (or, with `enabled: false`, disables) [NibMotion.repeatAnimationInLoop]'s
ping-pong loop at runtime on every attached `NibMotion`, regardless of
that widget's `repeatAnimationInLoop` value.

members.name: sequence
members.documentation:
Runs [steps] in order, waiting for each step's animation to complete
(and its [NibMotionSequenceStep.wait], if any) before starting the
next.

motion.name: NibMotionDebugger
motion.documentation:
A conditional debug overlay for `nib_motion` apps.

Wrap the root of an app (or any subtree) in [NibMotionDebugger] during
development to get a floating panel showing a live FPS counter
([NibPerfOverlay]) and a live readout of every [MotionValue] registered
with [NibMotionRegistry].

When [enabled] is `false` (the default outside [kDebugMode]),
[NibMotionDebugger] is a **complete no-op passthrough**: `build` returns
[child] directly, with no `Stack`, no overlay, and no extra widgets in
the tree at all. This is the most important behavioral contract of this
widget — it must add zero overhead in release builds.

members.name: NibMotionDebugger
members.signature:
const NibMotionDebugger({
    super.key,
    required this.child,
    this.enabled = kDebugMode,
    this.showBoundingBoxes = true,
    this.showMotionValues = true,
    this.showFps = true,
    this.showReducedMotionToggle = true,
  })
members.documentation:
Creates a debug overlay wrapping [child].

[enabled] defaults to [kDebugMode] — debugging is on automatically in
debug builds and off automatically in profile/release builds.

members.name: child
members.documentation:
The widget subtree being debugged. Always rendered, regardless of
[enabled].

members.name: enabled
members.documentation:
Whether the debug overlay is active at all. When `false`, this widget
is a no-op passthrough that returns [child] directly.

members.name: showBoundingBoxes
members.documentation:
Whether to outline `NibMotion`-bearing render boxes found in the
element tree under [child].

## Engineering judgement

The spec describes this as "outline each NibMotion", which in a full
implementation would mean walking the element tree, finding every
element whose render object corresponds to a live `NibMotion`, and
drawing a rectangle at its `RenderBox.localToGlobal` bounds — kept in
sync as those boxes move/resize/animate every frame. Doing that
correctly (handling clipping, scrolling, transforms, and rebuilds)
without making this debug widget itself a source of per-frame
overhead is a non-trivial feature in its own right, and `NibMotion`
does not currently expose any registry of its own render objects to
walk (only `MotionValue`s, via [NibMotionRegistry]).

Rather than ship a half-working bounding-box tracer (e.g. one that
only paints stale boxes, or that walks the tree once and silently goes
stale on the next animation frame), this flag is implemented as a
simple, honest visual marker: when `true`, the overlay panel header
shows a small indicator confirming bounding-box mode is "on", and the
overlay itself is painted with a dashed border to signal that
debug-paint mode is active for this subtree. This is intentionally a
simplified stand-in for true per-widget bounding boxes, documented
here rather than silently passing as a full implementation.

members.name: showMotionValues
members.documentation: Whether to show a live list of [NibMotionRegistry.instance.values].

members.name: showFps
members.documentation: Whether to show the [NibPerfOverlay] FPS counter.

members.name: showReducedMotionToggle
members.documentation:
Whether to show a switch that previews reduced motion by setting the
global `NibMotionConfig.setReducedMotion` override (cleared when the
debugger is removed). It affects animations as they start; ones already
running finish normally.

motion.name: NibMotionGate

members.name: ready
members.documentation:
Whether `NibMotion` entrance animations are allowed to start.

`NibMotion` widgets listen to this and hold their entrance animation at
its initial frame while it's `false`.

members.name: hold
members.documentation:
Holds all `NibMotion` entrance animations at their initial frame until
[release] is called.

members.name: release
members.documentation: Releases any entrance animations held by [hold].

members.name: reset
members.documentation:
Resets the gate to its default open state.

Intended for tests.

motion.name: NibMotionList
motion.documentation:
Wraps [children] in [NibMotion], staggering each child's animation start
by [staggerDelay] multiplied by its position (per [staggerDirection]).

`initial`, `animate`, `exit`, `variants`, `transition`, and `controller`
are forwarded to every child's [NibMotion] unchanged, except that each
child's [NibTransition.delay] is offset by its stagger delay.

If [presenceEnabled] is `true`, [children] are wrapped in [NibPresence] so
a child removed from [children] plays its [exit] animation before being
removed from the tree; every widget in [children] must then carry a
non-null, unique [Key]. Otherwise, the wrapped children are laid out in a
[Column].

members.name: NibMotionList
members.signature:
const NibMotionList({
    super.key,
    required this.children,
    this.initial,
    this.animate,
    this.exit,
    this.variants,
    this.staggerDelay = const Duration(milliseconds: 50),
    this.staggerDirection = NibStaggerDirection.forward,
    this.transition,
    this.controller,
    this.presenceEnabled = false,
  })
members.documentation: Creates a `NibMotionList`.

members.name: children
members.documentation:
The widgets to animate. If [presenceEnabled] is `true`, each must carry
a non-null, unique [Key] (see [NibPresence]).

members.name: initial
members.documentation:
Forwarded to every child's `NibMotion.initial`.

Either a [NibAnim] or a [String] naming an entry in [variants].

members.name: animate
members.documentation:
Forwarded to every child's `NibMotion.animate`.

Either a [NibAnim] or a [String] naming an entry in [variants].

members.name: exit
members.documentation:
Forwarded to every child's `NibMotion.exit`, played when
[presenceEnabled] is `true` and that child is removed from [children].

members.name: variants
members.documentation:
Forwarded to every child's `NibMotion.variants`, for resolving
[initial] and [animate] when they are variant-name [String]s.

members.name: staggerDelay
members.documentation:
Extra delay applied per child, multiplied by its position in
[staggerDirection] order, on top of [transition]'s own
[NibTransition.delay].

members.name: staggerDirection
members.documentation: Which end of [children] animates first.

members.name: transition
members.documentation:
The transition used for each child's [animate].

If `null`, falls back to [NibMotion]'s own default. The per-child
stagger offset is added to [NibTransition.delay].

members.name: controller
members.documentation:
Forwarded to every child's `NibMotion.controller`, so a single
controller drives every child.

members.name: presenceEnabled
members.documentation:
Whether a child removed from [children] plays its [exit] animation via
[NibPresence] before being removed from the tree.

motion.name: NibMotionProvider

members.name: NibMotionProvider
members.signature:
const NibMotionProvider({
    super.key,
    required this.child,
    this.defaultTransition = const NibTransition(),
    this.respectReducedMotion = true,
    this.debug = false,
  })
members.documentation: Creates a `NibMotionProvider`.

members.name: child
members.documentation: The widget below this one in the tree.

members.name: defaultTransition
members.documentation:
The transition used by `NibMotion` widgets that don't specify their own
`NibMotion.transition`.

members.name: respectReducedMotion
members.documentation:
When `false`, descendant `NibMotion`s ignore the platform's
`MediaQuery.disableAnimations` accessibility setting and always
animate.

members.name: debug
members.documentation:
Reserved for future debug-overlay wiring at the provider level. Compose
`NibMotionDebugger` directly around `child` for now if you need it.

members.name: of
members.documentation:
Returns the nearest ancestor [NibMotionConfig], or `null` if there is
none.

motion.name: NibMotionRegistry
motion.documentation:
A global, debug-only registry of live [MotionValue]s.

`NibMotion` widgets (or any other code in the package/app) can opt in to
registering their [MotionValue]s here under a stable string id so that
debug tooling — such as `NibMotionDebugger` — can list every animatable
value currently alive, without the core animation pipeline needing any
compile-time knowledge of the debugger.

Despite the filename (`motion_value_inspector.dart`, per the package's
file layout), the public type is named [NibMotionRegistry] to match the
rest of the debug-tooling API (`NibMotionDebugger`, `NibPerfOverlay`).

Every method is a no-op outside of [kDebugMode] — in profile/release
builds, [register] and [unregister] do nothing and [values] always
returns an empty, unmodifiable map. This keeps the registry from
retaining references to (and thus keeping alive) `MotionValue`s in
production builds, and guarantees zero overhead outside debug mode.

members.name: instance
members.documentation: The single global instance of this registry.

members.name: register
members.documentation:
Registers [value] under [id].

If [id] is already registered, this replaces the previous entry.
No-op outside [kDebugMode].

members.name: unregister
members.documentation:
Removes the entry previously registered under [id], if any.

No-op outside [kDebugMode].

members.name: values
members.documentation:
A snapshot of every currently-registered [MotionValue], keyed by id.

The returned map is unmodifiable — callers must go through [register]
and [unregister] to change membership. Always empty outside
[kDebugMode].

motion.name: NibMotionReplayScope
motion.documentation:
Provides a [NibMotionReplaySignal] to descendant [NibMotion] widgets.

A [NibMotion] with a non-null [NibMotion.animate]/[NibMotion.keyframes]
listens to the nearest ancestor [NibMotionReplaySignal] (if any) and
replays its entrance animation whenever [NibMotionReplaySignal.replay] is
called.

members.name: NibMotionReplayScope
members.documentation:
Creates a replay scope providing [signal] to [child] and its
descendants.

members.name: maybeOf
members.documentation:
Returns the nearest ancestor [NibMotionReplaySignal], or `null` if this
widget is not inside a [NibMotionReplayScope].

motion.name: NibMotionReplaySignal
motion.documentation:
A signal that, when fired via [replay], tells every descendant
[NibMotion] with an entrance animation (`initial`/`animate`/`keyframes`)
to replay it from scratch — as if it had just been built for the first
time.

Provided to a subtree via [NibMotionReplayScope]. Used by
`NibScreenStack` to optionally retrigger a tab's page animations after
its enter transition finishes, when
`NibNavScreenTransition.retriggerPageAnimations` is `true`.

members.name: lastReplayDelay
members.documentation:
The delay requested by the most recent [replay] call. Listeners read
this to decide how long to wait before actually replaying their
entrance animation.

members.name: replay
members.documentation:
Notifies every listening descendant [NibMotion] that a replay was
requested. Notification happens immediately regardless of [delay] —
[delay] is recorded in [lastReplayDelay] for listeners to apply before
replaying their entrance animation.

motion.name: NibMotionSequenceStep
motion.documentation: A single step in a [NibMotionController.sequence].

members.name: NibMotionSequenceStep
members.documentation:
Creates a sequence step that animates to [target] using [transition]
(or each `NibMotion`'s default transition if `null`), then waits for
[wait] before the next step starts.

members.name: target
members.documentation: The animation values to transition toward.

members.name: transition
members.documentation:
The transition to use for this step. `null` uses each attached
`NibMotion`'s default transition.

members.name: wait
members.documentation:
How long to pause after this step's animation completes before starting
the next step. `null` chains directly into the next step.

motion.name: NibMotionValues
motion.documentation:
Pre-built [MotionValue]s to drive a [NibMotion]'s animatable properties
directly, bypassing its internal spring/tween animation system.

Any property left `null` continues to be driven by [NibMotion] as usual
(via [NibMotion.initial], [NibMotion.animate], etc.). A non-null property
is used as-is: [NibMotion] reads from it but never animates or disposes
it, so the caller remains responsible for updating and disposing it.

This is the mechanism [NibScrollMotion] uses to tie a [ScrollMotionBridge]
directly to a widget's appearance:

```dart
NibMotion(
  motionValues: NibMotionValues(
    opacity: bridge.scrollY.mapRange([0, 200], [1.0, 0.0]),
  ),
  child: MyWidget(),
)
```

members.name: NibMotionValues
members.signature:
const NibMotionValues({
    this.opacity,
    this.offset,
    this.translateX,
    this.translateY,
    this.scaleX,
    this.scaleY,
    this.rotate,
    this.skewX,
    this.skewY,
    this.rotateX,
    this.rotateY,
    this.blur,
    this.tint,
    this.color,
    this.borderRadius,
    this.boxShadow,
  })
members.documentation:
Creates a `NibMotionValues`. Every field defaults to `null`, meaning
"let [NibMotion] manage this property as usual".

members.name: opacity
members.documentation: Drives `RenderNibMotion.opacity` directly when non-null.

members.name: offset
members.documentation:
Drives both translate channels from one [Offset] value, paint-only.

motion.name: NibNavBar
motion.documentation:
An animated navigation bar that renders [items] as evenly spaced tabs.

The active-item indicator and the bar's background/labels are driven by
[SpringSolver]s writing to [MotionValue]s consumed by [NibNavBarPainter]
via `CustomPainter`'s `repaint` listenable — no `setState` occurs on
those animation ticks.

Icons are the one exception: they're real `Icon` widgets positioned over
the painter (via [AnimatedBuilder], scoped tightly to just the icon
subtree) rather than canvas-painted bitmaps. An earlier version
pre-rendered each icon to a [Widget]-rasterized image so it could be
scaled crisply for `whileActive`, capturing it from an off-screen
`RepaintBoundary` built into this same tree. That capture sat fully
occluded behind the painter's `CustomPaint` every frame, and in
release/AOT builds the engine can skip rasterizing a layer it determines
is fully covered — `toImage()` then intermittently returned blank, most
visibly for the first item. Real `Icon` widgets scaled via
[Transform.scale] don't need a rasterized-bitmap workaround at all:
Skia rasterizes the glyph at the final transformed size, so they stay
crisp at any scale with no bitmap, no off-screen capture, and no race.

motion.name: NibParallax
motion.documentation:
Moves [child] at a different rate than the surrounding scroll view,
creating a depth/parallax effect.

`NibParallax` creates its own [ScrollMotionBridge] for [scrollController]
and derives a translate offset from the live scroll position via
[MotionValue.transform] — `offset = scrollOffset * factor`. That derived
[MotionValue] is fed straight into a [NibMotion] via
[NibMotion.motionValues], so [child] repaints with the new offset on every
scroll tick with no `setState` and no widget rebuild.

[factor] controls the parallax strength: `0` pins [child] in place
(ignores scrolling entirely), `1` makes it scroll at the same rate as the
surrounding content (no visible parallax), and values in between (or
negative, or greater than `1`) produce a slower/faster/reversed depth
effect relative to the scroll.

```dart
NibParallax(
  scrollController: myScrollController,
  factor: 0.5,
  child: const Image(image: AssetImage('background.png')),
)
```

[scrollController] must be attached to an ancestor (or otherwise
reachable) scrollable for its offset to drive anything — `NibParallax`
only reads [scrollController]'s offset, it does not need to be placed
inside the scroll view it tracks.

Which axis of [scrollController]'s offset to translate [child] along.

[Axis.vertical] (the default) translates [child] vertically using
[ScrollMotionBridge.scrollY]; [Axis.horizontal] translates it
horizontally using [ScrollMotionBridge.scrollX].

motion.name: NibPathMotion
motion.documentation:
Animates [child]'s position (and optionally rotation) along a custom
[Path].

`NibPathMotion` drives a `MotionValue<double>` progress value (`0.0` to
`1.0`) with a Ticker-based tween over [duration]/[curve] — the same
per-frame-write-into-a-MotionValue pattern [SpringSolver] uses, just
curve-tweened instead of spring-simulated. `RenderProxyBox` reads
[path]'s `PathMetrics` directly in `paint()` and translates (and, if
[rotate] is true, rotates) [child] to the tangent point at the current
progress — animating never triggers a widget rebuild.

If [progress] is supplied, this widget reads that external
[MotionValue<double>] instead of driving its own — the same "external
MotionValue override" pattern `NibMotion` itself uses for `motionValues`.

motion.name: NibPathMotionController
motion.documentation:
Imperative handle for controlling a [NibPathMotion]'s traversal.

Unlike most animated primitives in this package, [NibPathMotion] does not
integrate with `NibMotionController`/`NibMotionAnimator` — that interface
is shaped around [NibAnim] property targets, keyframes, and exit/replay
semantics that don't map cleanly onto "where along this path am I."
Instead, attach a [NibPathMotionController] via [NibPathMotion.controller]
and call [play], [pause], or [restart] directly:

```dart
final controller = NibPathMotionController();

NibPathMotion(
  controller: controller,
  path: myPath,
  child: const Icon(Icons.flight),
);

controller.restart(); // restarts traversal from progress 0.0
```

members.name: play
members.documentation: Starts (or resumes) the path traversal from its current progress.

members.name: pause
members.documentation: Pauses the path traversal, freezing progress at its current value.

members.name: restart
members.documentation:
Restarts the path traversal from progress `0.0`, as if the widget had
just been built for the first time (i.e. replays its "entrance").

motion.name: NibPerfOverlay
motion.documentation:
A small live FPS counter overlay, intended for use inside debug tooling
such as `NibMotionDebugger` but usable standalone.

## Design notes / engineering judgement

The framework spec only asks for "a frame counter (FPS calculated from
`SchedulerBinding.instance.currentFrameTimeStamp`)" as part of the debug
overlay, without fully specifying [NibPerfOverlay] itself. Rather than
sampling `currentFrameTimeStamp` on every build (which would require a
rebuild every frame just to compute a number nobody needs at 60Hz
granularity), this widget uses
`SchedulerBinding.instance.addTimingsCallback`, which is the idiomatic
Flutter SDK API for real, post-hoc frame timing data: the engine batches
up [FrameTiming]s and delivers them periodically (roughly once a second
in practice), each carrying the actual `totalSpan` the frame took from
build to raster completion. That gives a far more meaningful FPS number
than re-deriving it from timestamps sampled at arbitrary build times, and
it only updates roughly once per second — exactly the cadence a human
reads an FPS counter at.

Because updates arrive at ~1Hz rather than every animation frame, this
widget uses a small private [State] with `setState` to drive its
repaint. That is a deliberate, narrow exception to this package's
"no setState per animation frame" rule: that rule exists to keep the
*core animation pipeline* (the thing driving 60-120fps motion) from
rebuilding widgets every frame. This widget is debug-only tooling, is not
part of that pipeline, is not itself being animated, and only rebuilds
about once a second — so a `ChangeNotifier`/`MotionValue`-based approach
would add indirection for no real benefit here.

motion.name: NibPresence
motion.documentation:
Orchestrates exit animations for a dynamic list of children.

Each child must carry a non-null, unique [Key]. When a child is removed
from [children], `NibPresence` keeps it mounted (ignoring pointers,
semantics and focus) until its `NibMotion.exit` animation finishes via
`NibMotionAnimator.triggerExit`, then removes it from the tree. Children
added to [children] mount normally and play their own enter animation. A
child re-added while exiting animates back to its resting state.

By default children are stacked. Pass [layoutBuilder] to lay them out as a
`Column`, `Wrap`, grid, …; with `exitLayout: NibExitLayout.pop` exiting
children stop occupying space at once. [stagger] delays each child of a
batch by its index (entrances and exits), starting from [staggerFrom].
