A `NibPresence` whose children reflow with FLIP when one enters or
leaves — the common case wired up in one call.

It lays [children] out in a [Column], [Row] or [Wrap] ([axis]), wraps
them in a `NibLayoutScope`, and applies [childLayout] (default
[NibLayout.position]) to every child `NibMotion` that leaves its own
`layout` at [NibLayout.none] via `NibLayoutDefaults`. [exitLayout]
defaults to [NibExitLayout.pop], so siblings start closing the gap
immediately while the leaver fades out in place.

column or row pad the children.

motion.name: NibReorderable
motion.documentation:
A list whose items are reordered by long-press and drag, with the other
items gliding out of the way.

Built from the same runtime as everything else: every item is a
`NibMotion(layout: NibLayout.position)`, so when the dragged item crosses a
sibling the sibling FLIPs into its new slot (interruptible, velocity
preserving, reduced-motion aware). The dragged item follows the pointer with
a paint-time translation and springs into its slot on release.

Each of [children] needs a unique, non-null [Key]. [onReorder] is called once
on release with the item's original index and its final index (the index in
the resulting list, as after `ReorderableListView` adjusts it); update your
list there. If you do not, the items animate back.

Not scrollable itself: put it inside a scroll view on the same axis. While
an item is dragged near the leading or trailing edge of that scroll view it
scrolls automatically (faster the closer the pointer is to the edge).
Items are separated by [spacing]; the list runs along a single [axis].

Manages [screens] as a stack of always-mounted widgets, animating the

Reveals [child] with an animation when it scrolls into the viewport.

`NibScrollReveal` is a thin convenience wrapper over
[NibMotion.whileInView] — it configures [NibMotion.initial],
[NibMotion.whileInView], and [NibMotion.viewport] for the common "fade
and slide up on reveal" pattern, without reimplementing any
viewport-intersection logic.

```dart

)
```

logical pixels), animates to [animate] (`NibAnim.identity`, i.e. fully
visible at its natural position) once at least [amount] of its area is
visible, and — because [once] defaults to `true` — stays revealed even if
it's later scrolled back out of view.

motion.name: NibShaderEffect
motion.documentation:
Paints any fragment shader over (or masked by) [child], with
[MotionValue]s as live uniforms.

Changing a uniform repaints the layer; it never rebuilds the widget tree.

**Uniform layout** (the order your GLSL `uniform float` declarations must
follow):

1. `time` in seconds — only if [includeTime] (default `false`)
2. `width`, `height` in pixels — only if [includeSize] (default `true`)
3. one float per entry of [uniforms], in list order

Provide the shader either as a ready [program] or as an [asset] key loaded
through [NibShaderLoader.load] (declare it under `flutter: shaders:` in your
pubspec). While it loads, or if it fails to load or compile, [child] is
painted unchanged.

[blendMode] controls how the shader composites with the child: `srcOver`
(default) draws it on top; `srcIn` masks the shader to the child's alpha;
`multiply`, `screen` etc. tint it.

With [sampleChild] the shader *transforms the child's pixels* instead of
drawing over them: the child is rendered into a texture that the engine
binds to the shader's first `sampler2D`. This uses `ImageFilter.shader`, so
it needs Impeller; elsewhere (Skia, older engines) the child is painted
unchanged. The engine requires the shader's **first uniform to be a
`vec2`, which it overwrites with the texture size** — so [includeSize] must
stay `true`, and on the OpenGL ES backend the shader must flip the y axis
(see `ImageFilter.shader`). [blendMode] is ignored in this mode.

Reduced motion freezes [includeTime] at `0` (no ticker); uniforms you drive
yourself are unaffected.

```dart
final glow = MotionValue<double>(0);
NibShaderEffect(
  asset: 'shaders/glow.frag',
  includeTime: true,
  uniforms: [glow],
  blendMode: BlendMode.screen,
  child: card,
)
```

    required bool includeTime,
    required bool includeSize,
  })
members.documentation: The floats passed to the shader, in order. Exposed for tests.

motion.name: NibShaderLoader
motion.documentation:
A singleton cache/loader for the [FragmentProgram]s bundled with
`nib_motion`.

`FragmentProgram.fromAsset` compiles a shader asynchronously the first
time it's requested; widgets such as `NibShimmer` and `NibDissolve` call
straight into this loader and create their `FragmentShader` instances
once the relevant program resolves. Call [preloadAll] once at app
startup (via `NibMotionConfig.init`) so the first shader-backed widget
built doesn't pay the compilation cost on its own first frame.

members.name: assetKeyResolver
members.documentation:
Maps an asset key to the key actually passed to
`FragmentProgram.fromAsset`. `null` (the default) uses keys as-is.

Test-friendly: inside this package's own `flutter test` runs, the
bundled shaders resolve under the root-package key
(`lib/shaders/shimmer.frag`), not `packages/nib_motion/lib/shaders/…`
(which only exists in a consuming app). Set
`(key) => key.replaceFirst('packages/nib_motion/', '')` to exercise the
real shaders; [resetForTesting] clears it.

members.name: shimmer
members.documentation:
Returns the cached or newly-started [Future] that resolves to the
compiled [FragmentProgram] for the shimmer shader.

members.name: dissolve
members.documentation:
Returns the cached or newly-started [Future] that resolves to the
compiled [FragmentProgram] for the dissolve shader.

members.name: gradientSweep
members.documentation:
Returns the cached or newly-started [Future] that resolves to the
compiled [FragmentProgram] for the gradient sweep shader.

members.name: liquidGlass
members.documentation:
Returns the cached or newly-started [Future] that resolves to the
compiled [FragmentProgram] for the liquid-glass shader.

members.name: load
members.documentation:
Loads (and caches) any fragment program by [assetKey].

For your own shader declare it under `flutter: shaders:` in your app's
pubspec and pass its asset path (for a package asset,
`packages/<package>/<path>`). Used by `NibShaderEffect`.

members.name: preloadAll
members.documentation:
Kicks off compilation of every bundled shader and waits for all of
them to finish (or fail).

Failures are caught and swallowed here rather than rethrown: a host
app that doesn't bundle the shader assets (or runs in an environment
without shader compilation support, such as some test harnesses)
should still be able to start — shader-backed widgets fall back to
painting only their child when their program never resolves. Callers
that need to know whether preloading actually succeeded should call
[shimmer]/[dissolve]/[gradientSweep] directly and inspect the
resulting [Future].

members.name: resetForTesting
members.documentation:
Removes every cached program, forcing the next call to
[shimmer]/[dissolve]/[gradientSweep] to recompile from the asset.

Intended for tests.

motion.name: NibShake
motion.documentation:
Plays a rapid left-right shake animation on [child], commonly used for
input validation feedback.

The shake does not play automatically — trigger it on demand by calling
[NibShakeController.shake] on a controller passed to [controller]:

```dart
final shakeController = NibShakeController();

NibShake(
  controller: shakeController,
  child: const NibInput(...),
)

// Elsewhere, e.g. on validation failure:
shakeController.shake();
```

If [controller] is omitted, `NibShake` creates and owns one internally —
in that case, trigger the shake by wrapping `NibShake` in a widget that
has access to it via a [GlobalKey], or simply provide your own
[NibShakeController] when you need to trigger playback from outside this
widget.

members.name: NibShake
members.documentation: Creates a `NibShake`.

members.name: child
members.documentation: The widget to shake.

members.name: controller
members.documentation:
Triggers the shake animation via [NibShakeController.shake]. If `null`,
this widget creates and owns its own controller internally.

members.name: duration
members.documentation: How long one shake animation takes to play out.

motion.name: NibShakeController
motion.documentation:
Imperative handle for triggering [NibShake]'s shake animation on demand.

Call [shake] to play the shake animation once. Must be disposed via
[dispose] when no longer needed (unless owned internally by a
[NibShake] that was constructed without an explicit `controller`, which
disposes it automatically).

members.name: shake
members.documentation: Plays the shake keyframe animation once on every attached `NibShake`.

members.name: dispose
members.documentation: Releases this controller's resources. Safe to call once.

motion.name: NibSharedSource
motion.documentation:
Marks the widget a route grows out of (`sharedFrom`) so it can be hidden
while the route's content is standing in for it.

Wrap the source in a `NibSharedSource` and pass the same [sourceKey] to
`NibModalRoute`/`NibPageRoute`/`showNibDialog(sharedFrom:)`. While the
route is open the source keeps its layout space but paints nothing, so the
grown-out content is not drawn on top of its own thumbnail; it reappears
when the route has shrunk back over it.

Without a `NibSharedSource` (a plain `GlobalKey` on any widget) the hand-off
still animates; the source simply stays visible underneath.

```dart
final key = GlobalKey();
NibSharedSource(sourceKey: key, child: Thumbnail());
Navigator.push(context, NibPageRoute(sharedFrom: key, builder: ...));
```

members.name: NibSharedSource
members.documentation: Creates a source that can be hidden by a route using [sourceKey].

members.name: sourceKey
members.documentation:
The key to pass as `sharedFrom`. It is attached to this widget's box, so
the route measures the source's rectangle from it.

members.name: child
members.documentation: The widget the route grows out of.

motion.name: NibShimmer
motion.documentation:
Paints a GPU-accelerated diagonal shimmer sweep over [child].

`NibShimmer` is a drop-in, GPU-optimal replacement for the CSS-style
shimmer effect skeleton loaders typically build out of an
[AnimatedContainer]/gradient combo. The sweep position (`uTime`) is
driven by a raw [Ticker] writing into a [MotionValue<double>] — exactly
the pattern [SpringSolver] uses — so the running animation never causes
a widget rebuild; only [RenderNibShimmer.paint] is re-invoked.

If the bundled shimmer shader hasn't finished compiling yet (or fails to
compile, e.g. because the host app doesn't declare `nib_motion`'s
shaders as assets), [child] is painted as-is with no shimmer overlay.

members.name: NibShimmer
members.signature:
const NibShimmer({
    super.key,
    required this.child,
    this.baseColor,
    this.shimmerColor,
    this.speed = 1.5,
    this.angle = -0.3,
    this.enabled = true,
  })
members.documentation: Creates a shimmer overlay around [child].

members.name: child
members.documentation: The widget the shimmer sweep is painted over.

members.name: baseColor
members.documentation:
The background color the shimmer band is mixed over.

Defaults to the ambient theme's surface color when `null` (resolved as
`Theme.of(context).colorScheme.surface` is not available without a
Material dependency, so this resolves to a neutral light grey).

members.name: shimmerColor
members.documentation:
The highlight color of the sweeping band.

Defaults to a lighter tint of [baseColor] when `null`.

members.name: speed
members.documentation: How fast the shimmer band sweeps across [child], in sweeps per second.

members.name: angle
members.documentation: The sweep angle, in radians.

members.name: enabled
members.documentation:
Whether the shimmer animation is active.

When `false`, [child] is painted with no shimmer overlay and the
underlying [Ticker] is stopped.

motion.name: NibSimulationDriver
motion.documentation:
Runs any Flutter [flutter_physics.Simulation] (gravity, clamping scroll,
a custom decay…) on a [MotionValue<double>].

It follows the same contract as `SpringSolver`/`InertiaSolver`: it
publishes [MotionValue.velocity] every frame so a driver that takes over
continues the motion, and its future completes when the simulation is done
*or* superseded/stopped.

```dart
final driver = NibSimulationDriver(vsync: this, value: y);
await driver.run(GravitySimulation(2000, y.value, 600, 0));
```

members.name: NibSimulationDriver
members.documentation: Creates a driver writing to [value], ticking via [vsync].

members.name: onComplete
members.documentation: Called when a simulation finishes on its own (not when superseded).

members.name: isRunning
members.documentation: Whether a simulation is currently running.

members.name: run
members.documentation:
Starts [simulation], replacing any running one. Simulation time starts at
`0` on the first frame.

members.name: stop
members.documentation:
Freezes the value; velocity is kept for a following driver. The pending
future completes.

members.name: dispose
members.documentation: Stops and disposes the ticker. Safe to call more than once.

motion.name: NibSliverHeaderDelegate
motion.documentation:
A [SliverPersistentHeaderDelegate] that exposes how far the header has
collapsed as a [MotionValue] (`0.0` fully expanded → `1.0` fully collapsed)
instead of making you rebuild the header on every scroll frame.

[builder] runs **once**; the returned widget is reused as the sliver
re-lays the header out, and only [progress] changes. Pair it with
`NibMotion(motionValues: …)` and `mapRange` so the header repaints without
rebuilding:

```dart
SliverPersistentHeader(
  pinned: true,
  delegate: NibSliverHeaderDelegate(
    minExtent: 56,
    maxExtent: 220,
    builder: (context, progress) => NibMotion(
      motionValues: NibMotionValues(
        opacity: progress.mapRange([0, 1], [1, 0]),
      ),
      child: const Hero(),
    ),
  ),
)
```

[progress] is written while the sliver lays out, so listen with render
objects (`NibMotion`) or derived values, not `ValueListenableBuilder`
(which would call `setState` during layout).

members.name: NibSliverHeaderDelegate
members.documentation: Creates a delegate whose header goes from [maxExtent] to [minExtent].

members.name: builder
members.documentation: Builds the header content once; it receives [progress].

members.name: progress
members.documentation: Collapse progress: `0.0` fully expanded, `1.0` fully collapsed.

members.name: build
members.signature:
Widget build(
      BuildContext context, double shrinkOffset, bool overlapsContent)

motion.name: NibSliverProgress
motion.documentation:
Exposes the scroll-through progress of the sliver it is placed in as a
[MotionValue] — for a header inside a `SliverAppBar.flexibleSpace`, a
`SliverToBoxAdapter`, or any other sliver.

`progress` is `0.0` while the sliver's leading edge is at the viewport's
leading edge and reaches `1.0` after scrolling
`expandedExtent - collapsedExtent` pixels. It is computed synchronously
from the scroll position and the sliver's `precedingScrollExtent`, so there
is no one-frame lag and no rebuild: [builder] runs once.

Place it inside the sliver (as its child); it finds the nearest enclosing
[RenderSliver] and [Scrollable].

members.name: NibSliverProgress
members.documentation: Creates a progress source for the enclosing sliver.

members.name: expandedExtent
members.documentation: The sliver's full (expanded) main-axis extent.

members.name: collapsedExtent
members.documentation:
The extent it collapses to; progress reaches `1.0` when this much of the
difference has scrolled away.

members.name: builder
members.documentation: Builds the content once; it receives the progress value.

motion.name: NibSliverProgressBuilder
motion.documentation: Builds sliver-header content from a collapse-progress [MotionValue].

members.name: NibSliverProgressBuilder

motion.name: NibSpring
motion.documentation:
Named spring tokens, so an app describes motion by *role* instead of
scattering raw mass/stiffness/damping numbers.

The values are defined by NibMotion (each is a
[NibSpringDescription.fromDuration] of a perceptual duration and bounce);
they are **not** copies of Material 3 Expressive or Apple numbers. Two
families follow the usual split:

* `spatial*` — things that move or resize. A little overshoot is allowed.
* `effects*` — opacity/colour-like changes. Critically damped, never
  overshoot.

Each token has a matching [NibTransition] via [NibSpring.transition].

```dart
NibMotion(
  animate: const NibAnim(x: 100),
  transition: NibSpring.spatialDefault.transition,
)
```

Tokens are [NibSpringDescription]s. To pass one where a transition is
expected use `NibSpring.smooth.transition` (or
`NibTransition(spring: NibSpring.smooth)`).

members.name: spatialFast
members.documentation: Small, quick spatial movement (e.g. a chip nudge). ~300 ms, slight bounce.

members.name: spatialDefault
members.documentation: Default spatial movement. ~450 ms, gentle bounce.

members.name: spatialSlow
members.documentation: Large or deliberate spatial movement. ~700 ms, gentle bounce.

members.name: effectsFast
members.documentation: Quick non-spatial change (opacity, colour). ~150 ms, no overshoot.

members.name: effectsDefault
members.documentation: Default non-spatial change. ~250 ms, no overshoot.

members.name: effectsSlow
members.documentation: Slow non-spatial change. ~400 ms, no overshoot.

members.name: interactive
members.documentation: Tracks a finger or pointer: very quick, no overshoot. ~200 ms.

members.name: smooth
members.documentation: Clean and calm, no overshoot. ~500 ms.

members.name: snappy
members.documentation: Fast and decisive with a hint of overshoot. ~300 ms.

members.name: bouncy
members.documentation: Playful, clearly overshoots. ~550 ms.

motion.name: NibSpringCurve
motion.documentation:
A [Curve] that follows a spring's unit step response, so spring feel can be
used anywhere a curve is accepted — notably inside a time-parametrised
keyframe segment (`NibKeyframe.spring`).

The spring runs from `0` to `1` with zero initial velocity; its settling
time is stretched to exactly the curve's `0..1` domain, so the curve ends
on `1` (the final sliver of the tail is dropped) and overshoots above `1`
when the spring is underdamped.

members.name: NibSpringCurve
members.documentation: Creates a curve from [spring].

members.name: spring
members.documentation: The spring this curve samples.

motion.name: NibSpringDescription
motion.documentation:
Describes the physical properties of a spring used to drive a
[MotionValue] toward a target via [SpringSolver].

This wraps `package:flutter/physics.dart`'s `SpringDescription` and adds a
set of named presets so callers can write `NibSpringDescription.gentle`
instead of constructing raw mass/stiffness/damping values.

members.name: NibSpringDescription
members.documentation:
Creates a spring description.

- [mass] affects inertia. Higher values are slower to start and stop.
- [stiffness] is the spring tightness. Higher values are snappier.
- [damping] is the resistance. Higher values reduce oscillation.

[mass] and [stiffness] must be positive and finite, [damping] must be
non-negative and finite (`0` is an undamped spring). Violations fail an
assert in debug builds; in release builds [toFlutter] substitutes safe
values so a bad description can never poison a `MotionValue` with NaN.

members.name: NibSpringDescription.unchecked
members.documentation:
Creates a description **without** validation.

For tests and for code that has already validated its input; invalid
values are replaced by safe defaults in [toFlutter].

members.name: NibSpringDescription.fromDuration
members.documentation:
Creates a spring from how it should *feel* rather than raw physics.

[duration] is the perceptual duration (roughly how long until the motion
reads as settled) and [bounce] is in `-1.0..1.0`: `0` is critically
damped (no overshoot), positive values overshoot and oscillate, negative
values are overdamped and sluggish. Mass is fixed at `1`.

```dart
NibSpringDescription.fromDuration(
    duration: Duration(milliseconds: 450), bounce: 0.25)
```

members.name: gentle
members.documentation: A soft, slow-settling spring with minimal overshoot.

members.name: snappy
members.documentation: A tight, fast spring with very little overshoot.

members.name: wobbly
members.documentation: A loose spring that oscillates noticeably before settling.

members.name: stiff
members.documentation: A very tight, fast-settling spring with near-zero overshoot.

members.name: mass
members.documentation: The mass attached to the spring. Affects inertia.

members.name: stiffness
members.documentation: The spring constant. Higher values produce a snappier motion.

members.name: damping
members.documentation: The damping coefficient. Higher values reduce oscillation.

members.name: toFlutter
members.documentation:
Converts this description to a `package:flutter/physics.dart`
`SpringDescription` for use with `SpringSimulation`.

motion.name: NibSpringTransition
motion.documentation:
Adds [transition] to [NibSpringDescription] so tokens read
`NibSpring.smooth.transition`.

members.name: transition
members.documentation: A [NibTransition] driven by this spring.

motion.name: NibSpringTuner
motion.documentation:
A debug tool for tuning a spring by feel: sliders, a live preview driven by
a real [SpringSolver], the step-response curve (via [NibSpringCurve]) and a
copyable `NibSpringDescription(...)` snippet.

Widgets-only (no Material), so it drops into any debug overlay:

```dart
if (kDebugMode) NibSpringTuner(onChanged: (spring) => print(spring))
```

members.name: NibSpringTuner
members.documentation: Creates a tuner starting from [initial] in [mode].

members.name: initial
members.documentation:
The spring the tuner starts from. In [NibSpringTunerMode.durationBounce]
mode the duration/bounce sliders start at sensible values near it.

members.name: mode
members.documentation: Which parameter set is shown first.

members.name: onChanged
members.documentation: Called with the tuned spring whenever a slider moves.

motion.name: NibSpringTunerMode
motion.documentation: Which parameterisation [NibSpringTuner] edits.

members.name: durationBounce
members.documentation: Perceptual: duration and bounce ([NibSpringDescription.fromDuration]).

members.name: physical
members.documentation: Physical: mass, stiffness and damping.

motion.name: NibStaggerDirection
motion.documentation: Which end of [NibMotionList.children] animates first.

members.name: forward
members.documentation: The first child (index `0`) animates first.

members.name: reverse
members.documentation: The last child animates first.

motion.name: NibStaggerFrom
motion.documentation: Which end of the list a stagger starts from.

members.name: first
members.documentation: The first child goes first.

members.name: last
members.documentation: The last child goes first.

members.name: center
members.documentation: The middle child goes first, spreading outwards.

motion.name: NibSwipeDismiss
motion.documentation:
Swipes a widget horizontally (or vertically) to dismiss it, with a
threshold and spring-back.

Holds a single [MotionValue<double>] for the current offset along the
dismiss axis, written directly from `GestureDetector.onPanUpdate` and
read directly by a [RenderProxyBox] during `paint` — swiping never
triggers a widget rebuild. On release: if the offset exceeds
`dismissThreshold * extent`, the widget is animated off-screen via a raw
[Ticker]-driven decelerating tween and [onDismissed] is called; otherwise
it springs back to `0` using the release velocity.

members.name: NibSwipeDismiss
members.signature:
const NibSwipeDismiss({
    super.key,
    required this.child,
    required this.onDismissed,
    this.dismissThreshold = 0.5,
    this.dismissDirection = DismissDirection.horizontal,
    this.background,
    this.spring = NibSpringDescription.gentle,
  })
members.documentation: Creates a swipe-to-dismiss wrapper around [child].

members.name: child
members.documentation: The widget to make dismissible.

members.name: onDismissed
members.documentation:
Called once the widget has finished animating off-screen past
[dismissThreshold].

members.name: dismissThreshold
members.documentation:
The fraction of the widget's extent (width for horizontal directions,
height for vertical) the swipe must cross before release triggers a
dismissal instead of a spring-back.

members.name: dismissDirection
members.documentation: Which direction(s) of swipe are recognized.

members.name: background
members.documentation: A widget shown behind [child] (via a [Stack]) while swiping.

members.name: spring
members.documentation:
The spring physics used to animate back to `0` when the swipe doesn't
cross [dismissThreshold].

motion.name: NibText
motion.documentation:
Renders [text] (or [span]) split into independently animated character,
word, or line units (see [NibTextConfig.unit]), each staggered in by
[NibTextConfig.staggerDelay].

Each unit is wrapped in its own `NibMotion` driven by [config]'s
[NibTextConfig.initial]/[NibTextConfig.animate]/[NibTextConfig.exit], so
entrance, exit, and stagger all reuse the existing zero-setState
`NibMotion` animation engine — `NibText` itself never drives a per-frame
animation value.

members.name: NibText
members.documentation:
Creates a `NibText` that animates [text] split according to
`config.unit`.

members.name: NibText.rich
members.documentation:
Creates a `NibText` from a rich [InlineSpan] (e.g. a `TextSpan` with
mixed styles) instead of a flat [String]. The span's `toPlainText()` is
split into units; [style] is used as the base style for each unit and
per-span styling within [span] is not currently preserved per-unit.

members.name: text
members.documentation: The plain text to render and animate. Mutually exclusive with [span].

members.name: span
members.documentation: The rich span to render and animate. Mutually exclusive with [text].

members.name: config
members.documentation: Configures how the text is split into units and how each unit animates.

members.name: style
members.documentation: The base text style applied to every unit.

members.name: textAlign
members.documentation: Text alignment for the laid-out units.

members.name: overflow
members.documentation:
How to visually overflow text that doesn't fit, applied to each unit's
internal `Text`.

members.name: controller
members.documentation:
Forwarded to every unit's `NibMotion.controller`, so a single
`NibMotionController` can imperatively drive every unit at once.

motion.name: NibTextConfig
motion.documentation:
Configures how [NibText] splits and animates its text.

Each unit (character, word, or line — see [unit]) is wrapped in its own
`NibMotion` using [initial] as its starting state, [animate] as its target
state, and [exit] as its `NibPresence` exit state, staggered according to
[staggerDelay] and [staggerFrom].

members.name: NibTextConfig
members.signature:
const NibTextConfig({
    this.unit = NibTextUnit.character,
    this.initial,
    this.animate,
    this.exit,
    this.staggerDelay = const Duration(milliseconds: 30),
    this.staggerFrom = NibTextStaggerFrom.start,
    this.transition,
  })
members.documentation: Creates a text animation configuration.

members.name: unit
members.documentation: Whether to animate per-character, per-word, or per-line.

members.name: initial
members.documentation:
The starting state of each unit before its entrance. Defaults to
[NibAnim.identity] when `null`.

members.name: animate
members.documentation:
The target state of each unit at rest. When `null`, units render at
[initial] with no entrance animation.

members.name: exit
members.documentation:
The state each unit transitions to when the widget exits via an
ancestor `NibPresence`.

members.name: staggerDelay
members.documentation: The delay between each successive unit's animation start.

members.name: staggerFrom
members.documentation: Where stagger delay accumulates from — start, end, center, or random.

members.name: transition
members.documentation:
The transition used for each unit's entrance animation. Defaults to
`NibTransition.springGentle` with a 400ms tween fallback when no spring
is set.

members.name: copyWith
members.signature:
NibTextConfig copyWith({
    NibTextUnit? unit,
    NibAnim? initial,
    NibAnim? animate,
    NibAnim? exit,

motion.name: NibTextReveal
motion.documentation:
Reveals [child] (typically a block of text) by animating a clip mask that
wipes in from [direction] — the whole block reveals at once, with no
per-character splitting.

The clip's size factor is driven by a `MotionValue<double>` (`0.0` fully
clipped, `1.0` fully revealed) ticked by a `SpringSolver` (or a plain
`AnimationController`-driven tween when no spring is requested), and read
directly by `RenderNibTextReveal.paint` — the same zero-setState pattern
`RenderNibMotion` uses elsewhere in this package.

members.name: NibTextReveal
members.signature:
const NibTextReveal({
    super.key,
    required this.child,
    this.direction = NibTextRevealDirection.left,
    this.duration = const Duration(milliseconds: 500),
    this.delay = Duration.zero,
    this.curve = Curves.easeInOut,
    this.controller,
  })
members.documentation: Creates a `NibTextReveal` that wipes [child] into view from [direction].

members.name: child
members.documentation: The content being revealed.

members.name: direction
members.documentation: The edge the reveal wipes in from.

members.name: duration
members.documentation: How long the reveal animation takes.

members.name: delay
members.documentation: How long to wait before the reveal starts.

members.name: curve
members.documentation: The easing curve for the reveal.

members.name: controller
members.documentation:
An optional external handle for replaying the reveal via
[NibMotionController.start].

motion.name: NibTextRevealDirection
motion.documentation: The edge from which a [NibTextReveal] wipes its child into view.

members.name: left
members.documentation: Reveals left-to-right, clipping from the left edge.

members.name: right
members.documentation: Reveals right-to-left, clipping from the right edge.

members.name: up
members.documentation: Reveals bottom-to-top, clipping from the top edge.

members.name: down
members.documentation: Reveals top-to-bottom, clipping from the bottom edge.

motion.name: NibTextStaggerFrom
motion.documentation:
Where the per-unit stagger delay accumulates from, when [NibText] computes
each unit's entrance delay.

members.name: start
members.documentation: Delay increases from the first unit to the last: `index * staggerDelay`.

members.name: end
members.documentation:
Delay increases from the last unit to the first:
`(totalUnits - 1 - index) * staggerDelay`.

members.name: center
members.documentation: Delay increases outward from the middle unit toward both ends.

members.name: random
members.documentation:
Delay is a seeded-random value in `[0, totalUnits * staggerDelay)`, so
units animate in over the same overall window but in a shuffled order.

motion.name: NibTextUnit
motion.documentation: The granularity at which [NibText] splits its text into animated units.

members.name: character
members.documentation:
Each grapheme cluster (user-perceived character, including multi-code-unit
emoji) is its own animated unit.

members.name: word
members.documentation:
Each whitespace-delimited word is its own animated unit. Runs of
whitespace between words are preserved as plain (non-animated) text.

members.name: line
members.documentation: Each line (split on `\n`) is its own animated unit.

motion.name: NibTimeline
motion.documentation:
Plays a list of [NibTimelineEntry]s in time order, dispatching each
entry's `controller.start(target:, transition:)` at its [NibTimelineEntry.at]
offset from when [play] was called.

Use this to orchestrate multiple [NibMotionController]s (one per
animated element) against a single shared clock — think of it as a
playbook for a multi-element animation sequence.

```dart
final timeline = NibTimeline([
  NibTimelineEntry(controller: titleController, target: const NibAnim(opacity: 1), at: Duration.zero),
  NibTimelineEntry(controller: subtitleController, target: const NibAnim(opacity: 1), at: const Duration(milliseconds: 150)),
]);
await timeline.play();
```

members.name: NibTimeline
members.documentation:
Creates a timeline. Relative entries ([NibTimelineEntry.after],
[NibTimelineEntry.withStart]) are resolved to absolute times here, in
list order; an entry may only refer to a label defined *earlier* in
[entries].

members.name: entryDuration
members.documentation:
How long [entry] runs once started: its transition's delay plus its
duration (for springs, the time the spring takes to settle).

members.name: entries
members.documentation: The entries with all times resolved to absolute offsets, sorted by start.

members.name: duration
members.documentation: Total length: the latest entry end.

members.name: progress
members.documentation: Scrub position `0..1` last set by [seek]. [play] does not drive it.

members.name: seek
members.documentation:
Jumps every entry to the state it would have at [fraction] (`0..1`) of
[duration], without animating, and updates [progress].

Entries with a [NibTimelineEntry.from] are interpolated `from → target`
(using their curve, or the spring's settle curve). Entries without
`from` cannot be interpolated because their start state is unknown; they
step to their target once their end is reached. Entries that have not
started yet are set to `from` when they have one, otherwise left alone.

Scrubbing cancels any pending [play] timers.

members.name: play
members.documentation:
Schedules every entry's `controller.start(target:, transition:)` at its
[NibTimelineEntry.at] offset (via internal [Timer]s, so pending entries
can be cancelled by [pause]/[stop]).

Returns a [Future] that completes once the last entry has fired and its
animation has finished. Calling [play] again while already playing
cancels any still-pending entries from the previous run before
rescheduling all entries from this run.

members.name: pause
members.documentation:
Cancels every pending (not-yet-fired) entry, leaving already-started
animations running. The [Future] returned by [play] will never
complete after this is called, since the remaining entries won't fire.

members.name: stop
dispose
members.documentation:
Cancels all pending entries and marks this timeline as no longer
usable. Call this when the owner (e.g. a `State`) is disposed.

When the referenced entry (or the previous one) has *finished*, plus
[NibTimelineEntry.offset].

members.name: withStart
members.documentation: When the referenced entry *starts*, plus [NibTimelineEntry.offset].

motion.name: NibTimelineDragScrubber
motion.documentation:
Lets the user drag anywhere on [child] to scrub [timeline].

A drag along [axis] moves `timeline.progress` by `delta / extent`, through
the timeline's public [NibTimeline.seek], starting from wherever the
progress currently is (so repeated drags accumulate). Dragging stops any
running `play()`.

Horizontal scrubbing follows the ambient [TextDirection] unless
[respectTextDirection] is `false`: in RTL, dragging toward the leading
edge moves forward. [reverse] flips the direction on top of that.

Uses a horizontal-/vertical-drag recogniser (not pan) so scrollables on the
other axis keep working.

A single scheduled animation in a [NibTimeline].

Describes which [controller] to drive, what [target] to animate it to,
how (via [transition]), and when — either at an absolute offset ([at]) or
relative to another entry ([NibTimelineEntry.after],
[NibTimelineEntry.withStart]).

Relative entries are resolved to absolute times when the [NibTimeline] is
constructed. An entry's *end* is its start plus its transition's delay and
duration (for springs, the time the spring takes to settle).

motion.name: NibTypewriter

Reveals [text] character by character at [speed], with an optional
blinking [cursor].

This is the one widget in the text-animation system that legitimately
uses `setState`: the number of revealed characters is a discrete,
content-level value (not a per-frame paint value driven by a
`MotionValue`), advanced by a `Timer.periodic` — exactly the case the
package's zero-setState rule carves out an exception for. There is no
continuous animation here to drive through `MotionValue`/`RenderProxyBox`.

motion.name: NibValueBuilder
motion.documentation:
Springs a value of any [MotionConverter]-supported type toward [target] and
rebuilds [builder] as it moves.

Use it for things `NibMotion` does not animate because they change layout
(padding, size, alignment) or are arbitrary values (a `Rect`, a `Color`
fed to a painter). Changing [target] mid-flight retargets every axis from
its current position *and* velocity. Respects `NibMotionConfig` reduced
motion (the value jumps).

Unlike `NibMotion`, this rebuilds the builder subtree every frame; keep
the built subtree small, or prefer `NibMotion` for paint-only properties.

```dart
NibValueBuilder<EdgeInsets>(
  target: expanded ? const EdgeInsets.all(24) : EdgeInsets.zero,
  builder: (context, padding) => Padding(padding: padding, child: card),
)
```

Like the default constructor, but passes a prebuilt [child] through to
[childBuilder] so the static part of the subtree is built once and never
rebuilt while the value animates (the same idea as
`ValueListenableBuilder.child`).

```dart

  target: padding,
  child: const ExpensiveCard(),
  childBuilder: (context, p, child) => Padding(padding: p, child: child),
)
```

or a curve-based tween (`NibTransition(duration:, curve:)`, linearly

motion.name: NibVariants
NibViewportProgress
motion.documentation:
Reports how far its [child] has travelled through the viewport as
continuous values on [controller] — the continuous counterpart of
`NibMotion.whileInView`'s boolean.

Listens to **every** ancestor [Scrollable] (a horizontal list inside a
vertical page reports movement of either), measures against the nearest
one's viewport (or the screen when there is none), and only writes
[MotionValue]s: scrolling causes no rebuilds. Measurement runs after the
frame in which scrolling or layout changed, so values lag scrolling by at
most one frame.

Reverse-axis scrollables are measured in global screen direction, so
`progress` still means "leading edge enters first" in the direction the
content moves on screen only for forward axes; reversed lists report the
mirrored value.

```dart
final c = NibViewportProgressController();
NibViewportProgress(
  controller: c,
  child: NibMotion(
    motionValues: NibMotionValues(
      opacity: c.progress.mapRange([0, 0.3, 0.7, 1], [0, 1, 1, 0]),
    ),
    child: card,
  ),
)
```

child as [MotionValue]s, so any `NibMotion` (via `motionValues`) or
[MotionValue.mapRange] can react to it without rebuilding.

members.documentation:
Scroll-through progress along the scroll axis, `0..1`.

`0` when the child's leading edge is at the viewport's trailing edge (it
is just about to enter), `1` when the child's trailing edge has passed
the viewport's leading edge (it has fully left). It passes `0.5` when
the child is centred.

members.name: visibleFraction
members.documentation: Fraction of the child's area currently inside the viewport, `0..1`.

members.name: dispose

motion.name: NibVisibility
motion.documentation:
Shows or hides a single [child] with an enter/exit animation, keeping it
mounted until the exit has finished.

The one-widget counterpart of [NibPresence]: set [visible] to `false` and
the child fades (or whatever [exit] says) out *before* it is removed;
set it back to `true` mid-exit and the removal is cancelled and the child
animates back in from where it was. While exiting, the child ignores
pointers and is excluded from semantics and focus. Reduced motion
(`NibMotionConfig`) removes it immediately.

```dart
NibVisibility(
  visible: showBanner,
  initial: const NibAnim(opacity: 0, y: -12),
  exit: const NibAnim(opacity: 0, y: -12),
  transition: NibTransition.springSnappy,
  exitDelay: const Duration(milliseconds: 100),
  child: const Banner(),
)
```

Layout: the child sits in a [Stack] with default alignment, like
[NibPresence]; wrap in an `Align`/`Center` to position it.

motion.name: NibWaterController
motion.documentation:
Bounded water-body recovery and analytical wave state.

The owner must call [dispose]. The surface drives [advance]; do not attach
two independently ticking surfaces to one controller. No timer or ticker is
allocated here. Listeners receive one synchronous notification after a
completed mutation, and should invalidate painting rather than rebuild the
widget tree for each step.

Two connected Gaussian regions coalesce automatically while being moved.
The neck must exceed .52 (the visible contour is .5). Coalescence persists
after release; only [split] separates a body. An explicit split disables
automatic coalescence until another drag begins or [merge] is requested.
A body can belong to only one pointer at a time. Two separately owned bodies
do not coalesce until one pointer releases them.

This is a physically informed visual approximation. It does not implement
pressure, incompressibility, real surface tension, or 3D fluid volume.

members.name: NibWaterController
members.documentation:
Creates a controller with zero to ten decorative constituents.

Empty [drops] are useful for a continuous water surface. Configuration,
IDs, radii, positions and velocities are validated in release builds.

members.name: emitter
members.documentation:
Optional decorative emitter, advanced by this controller's existing clock.
Emitted bubbles stay independent; merge/split remains for manual droplets.

members.name: config
members.documentation: Current immutable configuration.

members.name: drops
members.documentation: Immutable snapshots of current constituent position, identity and speed.

members.name: impulses
members.documentation: Immutable snapshots of at most twelve live analytical wave impulses.

members.name: phase
members.documentation: Current coalescence/separation phase, updated before notifying listeners.

members.name: isActive
members.documentation:
Whether an advance can change positions or waves.

A motionless held pointer does not require continuous simulation work.

members.name: activeInputs
members.documentation: Number of pointers that currently own a decorative body.

members.name: massProxy
members.documentation:
Sum of constituent `pi * radius²`, in squared logical pixels.

Conserved between explicit scene replacement or emission operations. This is not the visible union area or 3D volume.

members.name: simulationTime
members.documentation: Accepted active simulation seconds; paused or discarded time is excluded.

members.name: lastStepMicros
members.documentation:
Wall-clock microseconds spent in the latest [advance], excluding listeners.

A diagnostic CPU measurement, not a frame/raster/GPU timing guarantee.

members.name: isReducedMotion
members.documentation: Whether motion reduction currently resolves changes without animation.

members.name: isDisposed
members.documentation: Whether the owner has disposed this controller.

members.name: configure
members.documentation: Applies validated settings without resetting bodies, impulses or time.

members.name: advance
members.documentation:
Advances linear simulation time by at most 66 milliseconds per call.

Larger gaps are discarded, not accumulated for a catch-up burst. Each
accepted interval is divided into steps no larger than 1/120 second.
[seconds] must be finite and nonnegative. Zero or idle advances do nothing.
Critical spring recovery preserves current velocity when retargeted and
caps velocity/displacement at 4000 logical pixels per second.

members.name: setDrops
members.documentation:
Replaces the decorative scene in one notification; IDs remain caller-owned.
At most ten validated bodies. Existing pointer ownership is cancelled.
Reset restores the constructor's original scene. Do not combine with an emitter.

members.name: putDrop
members.documentation: Adds or moves one decorative body, preserving other body snapshots.

members.name: removeDrop
members.documentation: Removes a decorative body by stable ID; no change if it is absent.

members.name: setEmitting
members.documentation: Starts or stops emission without changing the simulation clock.

members.name: disturb
members.documentation:
Adds a bounded disturbance at [center] in receiver-local logical pixels.

Strength is in 0..24; zero strength and reduced motion create no impulse.
The thirteenth impulse replaces the oldest. Impulses expire at amplitude
below .01 or after eight active simulation seconds, whichever is first.

members.name: fieldAt
members.documentation:
Returns the visible Gaussian field value at a receiver-local point.

Each constituent contributes `exp(-ln(2) * distance² / radius²)`.
The renderer's contour threshold is .5. This value is not a fluid height.

members.name: hitTest
members.documentation:
Returns the nearest contributing constituent ID inside the .5 contour.

Returns null outside the visible field. This is a decorative handle hit
test; it must not be used to combine independently actionable UI controls.

members.name: beginDrag
members.documentation:
Claims the body hit at [point] for [pointer], without moving it.

Returns false for a missed hit, a reused pointer, or an already owned body.
The grab offset is retained: subsequent [dragTo] calls move the existing
target by the pointer delta rather than jumping its center to the pointer.

members.name: dragTo
members.documentation:
Retargets the owned body by a receiver-local pointer delta.

An unknown pointer is ignored. Position and velocity stay continuous until
[advance], except under reduced motion, which resolves the target at once.

members.name: endDrag
members.documentation:
Releases ownership, allowing recovery to the last pointer target.

Cancellation removes pointer translation and clears velocities. A singleton
freezes in place; a merging body continues recovery toward its current
centroid, and a splitting body retains its separation targets. A normal
release preserves velocity and the target. Neither path implicitly splits.

members.name: cancelInputs
members.documentation:
Cancels all active owners without leaving latent pointer targets.

Impulses and bodies that have no owner continue their current recovery.

members.name: merge
members.documentation:
Coalesces all constituents toward their area-weighted centroid.

This explicit command releases pointer ownership. Centers and velocities
remain continuous while body identity changes before notification.

members.name: split
members.documentation:
Continuously separates each body's constituent regions.

Initial relative positions are centered on the body's current centroid
and expanded until pairwise separation is at least 1.7 times the sum of
radii. Coincident or unrepresentable initial layouts use deterministic
horizontal ordering. A common translation keeps all targets inside the
coordinate bounds without collapsing their separation.
The small extra gap provides hysteresis beyond the visible merge neck.
Identities separate on settlement, and automatic merging stays disabled
until the next drag or explicit merge. This command cancels ownership,
but preserves instantaneous position and velocity unless motion is reduced.

members.name: reset
members.documentation:
Restores original drops/velocities and clears inputs, waves and time.

Current settings and reduced-motion preference are retained. Reduced
motion also resolves any initially shared body to its final center.

members.name: setReducedMotion
members.documentation:
Applies motion reduction, which takes precedence over active motion.

Enabling it clears waves, resolves current targets, zeros velocities and
finishes merge/split synchronously. Disabling it does not replay old work.

motion.name: NibWaterDrop
motion.documentation:
An immutable constituent of a decorative water body.

Radius remains unchanged during merge and split. The conserved quantity is
the sum of `pi * radius * radius`, not the union silhouette area or 3D volume.

IDs must be unique within a controller. Radius must be in 8..256 and each
center coordinate in -1,000,000..1,000,000. Initial velocity is accepted
up to 4000 logical pixels per second. Values are checked by the controller.
Matching [bodyId] values declare an initially shared body; the controller
canonicalizes each body's identity to its lowest constituent ID.

motion.name: NibWaterSurface
motion.documentation:
Optical water over a designated Flutter background subtree.

Requires finite bounds. [sampling] defaults to the recoverable legacy
asynchronous path. Opt into [NibWaterSampling.live] for composition-time
layer sampling at device-relative [quality]. Static and throttled policies
explicitly trade freshness for work. The candidate retains one input image
and one output picture; engine intermediates are outside its input budget.
Platform views and content outside [background] are unsupported. Refraction
clamps to local image edges; provide padded content when needed. No offscreen
neighbors or inverse-warp hit-testing are inferred.

One surface drives one [controller] in receiver-local logical pixels. The
caller disposes the controller. This widget owns its shader and images.
[child] remains sharp and keeps its own semantics. TickerMode, [paused] and
app backgrounding suspend work; wall time is discarded on resume.

Drives a [MotionValue<double>] toward a target using real spring physics.

`SpringSolver` runs a [flutter_physics.SpringSimulation] on a [Ticker] and
writes the simulated position to [value] on every tick. Because
`MotionValue.value` notifies listeners directly (and `RenderNibMotion`
responds by calling `markNeedsPaint()`), this entire chain runs without
`setState` or widget rebuilds.

members.name: animateTo
members.documentation:
Starts (or restarts) the spring simulation toward [target].

The simulation starts from the current [MotionValue] position and
[MotionValue.velocity], so a spring taking over from any other driver
(a previous spring, a tween, inertia, a drag) continues that motion
instead of restarting from rest. Pass [from] to start elsewhere (with
zero velocity) and [initialVelocity] to override the inherited velocity.

The returned future completes when the spring settles, or when this
animation is superseded by another [animateTo] or by [stop]/[dispose].

members.name: stop
members.documentation:
Stops the simulation immediately, freezing [value] at its current
position. [MotionValue.velocity] is left intact so a driver that takes
over continues the motion; the pending [animateTo] future completes.

members.name: dispose
members.documentation:
Stops and disposes the underlying [Ticker]. Safe to call whether or not
an animation is running.

motion.name: computeAnimFromKeyframes
motion.documentation:
Computes the [NibAnim] at progress [t] along [keyframes].

[keyframes] is sorted by [NibKeyframe.at] first if it isn't already.

- If [t] is at or before the first keyframe, returns its [NibKeyframe.value]
  directly.
- If [t] is at or after the last keyframe, returns its [NibKeyframe.value]
  directly.
- Otherwise, finds the two keyframes surrounding [t], normalizes [t] into
  that segment, applies the upcoming keyframe's [NibKeyframe.curve] (or
  [defaultCurve] if unset), and interpolates between the two keyframes'
  values with [NibAnim.lerp].

components.name: NibAccordion
components.documentation:
A vertically stacked set of expandable [items].

Unlike Flutter's `ExpansionTile`, it has built-in **single-open
coordination**: by default opening one section closes the others. Set
[allowMultipleOpen] to let several stay open at once, and [defaultOpenIndex]
to start with one expanded.

```dart
NibAccordion(items: [
  NibAccordionItem(title: Text('Shipping'), content: Text('…')),
  NibAccordionItem(title: Text('Returns'), content: Text('…')),
])
```

Expansion is instant by default; set [animated] to reveal with a height
animation and a `nib_motion` chevron rotation. Drive it programmatically with
a [NibAccordionController].

    this.controller,
    this.allowMultipleOpen = false,

    this.onExpansionChanged,

internally when this is `null`, disposing it on unmount/controller-swap.

Whether more than one section may be open at once. `false` (default) closes
siblings when one opens.

members.documentation:

instantly and builds zero `NibMotion`.

required for basic use — the accordion creates and owns one internally when
none is supplied, and disposes it on unmount/controller-swap.

It also encapsulates the **single-open coordination** that `ExpansionTile`
lacks: with [allowMultiple] `false` (the default), opening one section closes
the rest. Read [openIndices] (it's a [ChangeNotifier], so you can listen) and
drive it with [open]/[close]/[toggle]/[openAll]/[closeAll].

Declarative face of the bottom sheet, matching the house style of
`NibDialog` / `NibSelect`: a [trigger] whose tap opens a modal sheet, with
open/closed state managed internally (or via an optional [controller]). Built
on the same [openNibBottomSheet] primitive as [showNibBottomSheet].

Simplest usage needs only [trigger] and [content]:

```dart
NibBottomSheet(
  trigger: const Text('Open'),
  title: 'Options',
  content: const Text('…'),
)
```

The [trigger] is wrapped so a tap opens the sheet — pass a non-interactive
widget (text, icon, a custom chip). For a fire-and-forget sheet that returns
a result, prefer [showNibBottomSheet] instead.

programmatic snapping. Never required for basic use — `NibBottomSheet`

disposes it on unmount/controller-swap.

(a menu item, a keyboard shortcut) or to move an open sheet between its snap
points. For the imperative `showNibBottomSheet` entry point there is no
controller — its returned `Future`/`NibBottomSheetHandle` plays that role.

components.name: NibBreadcrumb
components.documentation:
A navigation trail that auto-collapses its middle items into an ellipsis /
overflow menu when there are too many crumbs or the viewport is too narrow.

Simple by default — `NibBreadcrumb(items: [...])` — with the last item shown
as the current page. Collapsing is driven by [maxVisibleItems] **and** the
available width; the hidden crumbs open in a [NibPopover] from the `…`.

```dart
NibBreadcrumb(items: [
  NibBreadcrumbItem(label: 'Home', onTap: goHome),
  NibBreadcrumbItem(label: 'Docs', onTap: goDocs),
  NibBreadcrumbItem(label: 'Breadcrumb'), // current
])
```

components.name: NibButton
components.documentation:
A native, token-driven button.

Simple by default — `NibButton(label: 'Save', onPressed: ...)` already looks
finished — with five [NibButtonVariant]s, three [NibButtonSize] presets, and
opt-in `nib_motion` on tap.

All variants share identical box geometry for a given size: a filled and an
outline button of the same `height`/`width` render at the **same** footprint
and inner content position, because every variant reserves the same 1px
border inset (drawn *inside* the bounds) and the focus ring is a
layout-neutral overlay.

```dart
NibButton(label: 'Save', onPressed: () {})                       // primary
NibButton(label: 'Cancel', variant: NibButtonVariant.outline, onPressed: () {})
NibButton(onPressed: () {}, leadingIcon: Icon(Icons.add), semanticLabel: 'Add')
```

`InkWell`. `false` (the default) renders a plain static container.

members.name: onTap
members.documentation: Called on tap when [interactive] is true. `null` renders it disabled.

members.name: disabled
members.documentation: Disables interaction and dims the card regardless of [onTap].

members.name: semanticLabel
members.documentation: Accessible name for the whole card.

members.name: animated
members.documentation:
Opt-in `nib_motion`: a press scale-pop on [interactive] cards. `false`
(or a non-interactive card) builds **zero** [NibMotion].

members.name: transition
members.documentation: Timing/curve for [animated]. `null` → a short ~150ms ease.

components.name: NibCarousel
components.documentation:
A swipeable carousel of [items] with an optional dots/line indicator,
auto-play (paused while the user is interacting), a "peek" of the adjacent
slides, and infinite [loop] scrolling.

Built on a native [PageView] — physics, accessibility, and pointer handling
come for free. Usable with just [items]:

```dart
NibCarousel(items: [Card1(), Card2(), Card3()])
```

Drive it programmatically with a [NibCarouselController]; animation of the
active indicator is opt-in via [animated] (nothing routes through
`nib_motion` when it's `false`).

members.name: NibCarousel
members.signature:
const NibCarousel({
    super.key,
    required this.items,
    this.controller,
    this.height = 220,
    this.autoPlay = false,
    this.autoPlayInterval = const Duration(seconds: 4),
    this.loop = false,
    this.peekExtent = 0,
    this.viewportFraction,
    this.indicatorStyle = NibCarouselIndicatorStyle.dots,
    this.padEnds = true,
    this.onPageChanged,
    this.animated = false,
    this.transition,
  })

members.name: items
members.documentation:
The slides. Each is laid out to fill the carousel's [height] and viewport
width (minus any [peekExtent]).

members.name: controller
members.documentation:
Optional external controller. Never required — `NibCarousel` owns one
internally when this is `null`, disposing it on unmount/controller-swap.

members.name: height
members.documentation: The carousel's fixed height.

members.name: autoPlay
members.documentation:
Whether the carousel advances on its own. Pauses while the user drags and,
when [loop] is `false`, stops at the last slide.

members.name: autoPlayInterval
members.documentation: Delay between auto-play advances.

members.name: loop
members.documentation: Whether scrolling wraps around infinitely (last → first and back).

members.name: peekExtent
members.documentation:
Logical pixels of the neighbouring slides to reveal on each side. Converted
to a [PageView.viewportFraction] against the measured width. Ignored when
[viewportFraction] is set.

members.name: viewportFraction
members.documentation:
Explicit [PageView.viewportFraction] override (`1.0` = full width). Takes
precedence over [peekExtent].

members.name: indicatorStyle
members.documentation: How to draw the page indicator (or [NibCarouselIndicatorStyle.none]).

members.name: padEnds
members.documentation:
Forwarded to [PageView.padEnds] — whether the first/last slides are padded
to centre when peeking.

members.name: onPageChanged
members.documentation: Called with the new logical page index whenever the visible slide changes.

members.name: animated
members.documentation:
Opt-in `nib_motion` animation of the active indicator. `false` builds zero
`NibMotion`.

members.name: transition
members.documentation:
Timing/curve for the [animated] indicator pop. `null` → a short ~220ms
ease.

components.name: NibCarouselController
components.documentation:
Optional external controller for a [NibCarousel]'s current page. Never
required for basic use — the carousel creates and owns one internally when
none is supplied, and disposes it on unmount/controller-swap.

Read the live page via [page] (it's a [ChangeNotifier], so you can listen),
and drive it with [nextPage]/[previousPage]/[animateToPage]/[jumpToPage].

members.name: page
members.documentation: The current logical page index (0-based, independent of loop wrapping).

members.name: nextPage
members.documentation:
Advances one slide (wrapping when the carousel loops; a no-op at the last
slide otherwise).

members.name: previousPage
members.documentation:
Goes back one slide (wrapping when the carousel loops; a no-op at the first
slide otherwise).

members.name: animateToPage
members.documentation: Animates to a specific logical page.

members.name: jumpToPage
members.documentation: Jumps to a specific logical page without animation.

components.name: NibCarouselDot
components.documentation:
A single page-indicator mark for a [NibCarousel]. Public so a consumer's
tests can count them; you rarely construct one directly.

members.name: line
members.documentation: A row of short pills; the active page's pill is elongated.

components.name: NibCheckbox
components.documentation:
A single tri-state checkbox — mirrors Flutter's own [Checkbox] contract
([tristate], the false → true → null → false tap cycle, `mixed` semantics
for the indeterminate state) built to Nib's design tokens, with optional
built-in label/description slots for a full-row tap target.

```dart
NibCheckbox(value: checked, onChanged: (v) => setState(() => checked = v))
NibCheckbox(
  value: checked,
  label: 'Accept terms',
  onChanged: (v) => setState(() => checked = v!),
)
```

components.name: NibCircularLoader
components.documentation:
A custom-painted indeterminate circular loader — a soft full-circle track
with a gradient sweep and rounded caps rotating over it, and an optional
[child] centred inside (an icon, a short label, a logo).

Deliberately richer than Flutter's thin `CircularProgressIndicator`: the
sweep fades in from transparent to [color] so it reads as a comet tail, and
the stroke is thick with round caps. Reusable anywhere; `NibOtpInput` shows
one in its keypad's confirm slot while verifying.

```dart
NibCircularLoader(size: 56, child: Icon(Icons.lock_outline))
```

components.name: NibCombobox
components.documentation:
A native combobox: a text field fused with a filtered, keyboard-navigable
dropdown of [NibComboboxOption]s. Supports type-to-filter, single- and
multi-select (chips shown inside the field), free-text vs. selection-only
modes, and both synchronous ([options]) and async/debounced
([asyncOptionsLoader]) data sources with an in-dropdown loading state.

Simplest usage needs only [options]:

```dart
NibCombobox<String>(
  options: const [
    NibComboboxOption(value: 'apple', label: 'Apple'),
    NibComboboxOption(value: 'banana', label: 'Banana'),
  ],
  onChanged: (value) => print(value),
)
```

members.name: NibCombobox
members.signature:
const NibCombobox({
    super.key,
    this.options = const [],
    this.asyncOptionsLoader,
    this.multiSelect = false,
    this.allowFreeText = false,
    this.debounceDuration = const Duration(milliseconds: 300),
    this.onChanged,
    this.onSelectionChanged,
    this.onFreeTextSubmitted,
    this.loading = false,
    this.filter,
    this.noResultsBuilder,
    this.placeholder = 'Select…',
    this.clearable = true,
    this.disabled = false,
    this.animated = false,
    this.transition,
    this.maxDropdownHeight = 280,
    this.controller,
    this.backgroundColor,
    this.borderColor,
    this.borderWidth,
    this.borderRadius,
    this.padding,
    this.hintStyle,
  })

members.name: options
members.documentation:
The synchronous option list. Ignored while [asyncOptionsLoader] is set
(that loader becomes the data source instead).

members.name: asyncOptionsLoader
members.documentation:
Async data source. When set, options are (re)loaded — debounced by
[debounceDuration] — on each query change, with an in-dropdown spinner
while pending and a stale-response guard so only the latest request's
result is applied.

members.name: multiSelect
members.documentation:
Multi-select mode: picks toggle, the dropdown stays open, and selected
values render as removable chips inside the field.

members.name: allowFreeText
members.documentation:
When `true`, text that doesn't match an option can still be committed
(Enter) — reported via [onFreeTextSubmitted]. When `false` (default), the
value only ever changes by picking an option; typing that doesn't match
reverts on close.

members.name: onChanged
members.documentation:
Single-select convenience: fires the newly-selected value (or `null` when
cleared). For multi-select use [onSelectionChanged].

members.name: onSelectionChanged
members.documentation: Fires the full selection list on every selection change, in both modes.

members.name: onFreeTextSubmitted
members.documentation:
Fires the raw text when [allowFreeText] is on and the user commits text
that isn't an option.

members.name: loading
members.documentation:
Consumer-forced loading state — shows the in-dropdown loading indicator
without using [asyncOptionsLoader] (for callers driving their own async).

members.name: filter
members.documentation:
Overridable local match predicate. Defaults to [defaultComboboxFilter]
(case-insensitive substring on label/subtitle). Not used on the
[asyncOptionsLoader] path (the loader owns matching there).

members.name: noResultsBuilder
members.documentation:
Builds the dropdown body when there are no results and nothing is
loading. Defaults to a muted "No results" row.

members.name: clearable
members.documentation:
Whether to show the trailing clear (✕) button when there's a query or
selection to clear.

members.name: animated
members.documentation:
Opt-in dropdown entrance animation via `nib_motion`. `false` allocates
zero `NibMotion`/`MotionValue` overhead.

members.name: transition
members.documentation:
Transition used when [animated] is `true`. `null` falls back to a short
fade+scale+slide.

members.name: controller
members.documentation:
Optional external controller for selection/query/open state. Never
required — `NibCombobox` creates and owns one internally when this is
`null`, and disposes it on unmount/controller-swap.

members.name: backgroundColor
members.documentation:
Fill color of the field (and the dropdown card, so both read as one
surface). `null` ⇒ [NibTheme.background] for the field (or
[NibTheme.muted] while [disabled]) and [NibTheme.card] for the dropdown.

members.name: borderColor
members.documentation:
Border color of the field. `null` ⇒ [NibTheme.ring] while open,
otherwise [NibTheme.border].

members.name: borderWidth
members.documentation: Border thickness of the field. `null` ⇒ `1`.

members.name: borderRadius
members.documentation: Corner radius of the field. `null` ⇒ [NibTheme.radiusDefault].

members.name: padding
members.documentation: Inner content padding of the field. `null` ⇒ a sensible default.

members.name: hintStyle
members.documentation:
Style of the [placeholder] hint. Merged onto the default (which uses
[NibTheme.mutedForeground]).

components.name: NibComboboxController
components.documentation:
Optional external controller for a [NibCombobox]'s selection, query text,
and open/closed state. Never required for basic use — `NibCombobox`
creates and owns its own controller internally when none is supplied, and
disposes it on unmount/controller-swap. Pass an explicit instance to read
or drive the combobox from elsewhere in the tree (e.g. a "clear filters"
button, or reading the current selection for a form).

members.name: selectedValues
members.documentation:
The currently-selected values, in selection order (a single-element list
in single-select mode). Unmodifiable — mutate via [selectOnly] /
[toggle] / [clear].

members.name: selectedValue
members.documentation:
Convenience accessor for single-select use: the first selected value, or
`null` if nothing is selected.

members.name: query
members.documentation:
The current query text mirrored from the field. Read-only here; set it
through the field itself.

members.name: isOpen
members.documentation: Whether the dropdown is currently open.

members.name: selectOnly
members.documentation: Replaces the whole selection with just [value] (single-select semantics).

members.name: toggle
members.documentation: Adds [value] if absent, removes it if present (multi-select semantics).

members.name: clear
members.documentation: Clears the whole selection.

members.name: setQuery
members.documentation:
Mirrors the field's current query text into the controller so external
readers see it. Called by the widget on each text change; does not notify
by default since the widget already rebuilds itself on text change.

components.name: NibComboboxFilter
components.documentation:
Overridable match predicate used by [NibCombobox]'s local filtering —
`true` if [option] should remain visible for the current [query].

members.name: NibComboboxFilter
members.signature:
typedef NibComboboxFilter<T> =
    bool Function(NibComboboxOption<T> option, String query);

components.name: NibComboboxOption
components.documentation:
One selectable entry in a [NibCombobox].

[value] is the typed payload reported through the change callbacks and the
controller; [label] is the human-readable text shown in the list, used as
the field's text once selected, and matched against by the default filter.

members.name: NibComboboxOption
members.signature:
const NibComboboxOption({
    required this.value,
    required this.label,
    this.subtitle,
    this.icon,
    this.disabled = false,
  })

components.name: NibComboboxOptionsLoader
components.documentation:
Async data source for a [NibCombobox]: given the current [query], resolves
the options to show. Called (debounced) on each query change; the widget
shows an in-dropdown loading row while the future is pending and guards
against stale responses (only the latest request's result is applied).

components.name: NibCommandAction
components.documentation:
One entry in a [NibCommandPalette]'s action list.

An action with non-empty [children] is a branch: selecting it drills the
palette into those children instead of firing selection (e.g. "Change
theme" -> "Light" / "Dark" / "System"). A leaf action (no children) fires
its own [onSelected] and the palette's `onActionSelected`, then closes.

members.name: NibCommandAction
members.signature:
const NibCommandAction({
    required this.id,
    required this.label,
    this.subtitle,
    this.icon,
    this.shortcutLabel,
    this.group,
    this.children = const [],
    this.onSelected,
    this.disabled = false,
  })

members.name: id
members.documentation:
Stable identifier, used for recent-action tracking and as a default
list key.

members.name: shortcutLabel
members.documentation: Display-only shortcut hint (e.g. `'⌘S'`) — not a real key binding.

members.name: group
members.documentation:
Section-header key. Actions sharing the same [group] are clustered
together in display order; `null` renders with no header.

members.name: children
members.documentation:
Sub-actions revealed when this action is selected. Non-empty makes
this a branch rather than a leaf.

components.name: NibCommandActionFilter
components.documentation:
Overridable match predicate used by [NibCommandPalette]'s filtering —
`true` if [action] should remain visible for the current [query].

members.name: NibCommandActionFilter
members.signature:
typedef NibCommandActionFilter =
    bool Function(NibCommandAction action, String query);

components.name: NibCommandPalette
components.documentation:
A native command palette: wraps [child] and shows a searchable,
keyboard-navigable action list in a centered overlay, triggered by a
global keyboard shortcut (default `Cmd+K` on macOS/web-on-mac, `Ctrl+K`
elsewhere) or programmatically via [controller].

Simplest usage needs only [actions] and [child]:

```dart
NibCommandPalette(
  actions: [
    NibCommandAction(id: 'new-file', label: 'New File'),
  ],
  child: MyAppContent(),
)
```

members.signature:

    required this.child,
    required this.actions,

overlay lives in a separate [OverlayEntry].

members.name: actions

members.name: openShortcut

The global shortcut that opens the palette. Defaults to
[defaultOpenShortcut] (platform-aware Cmd+K/Ctrl+K). Fires regardless
of where focus currently is, and never blocks the host app's own
bindings for any other key combination.

members.name: filter
members.documentation:
Overridable match predicate. Defaults to [defaultCommandActionFilter]
(case-insensitive substring match on label/subtitle).

members.name: onActionSelected

Fires for every leaf-action selection, in addition to that action's
own [NibCommandAction.onSelected].

members.name: showRecent

Whether a "Recent" section is shown at the root level when the query
is empty and history is non-empty.

members.name: maxRecent

members.name: animated
members.documentation:
Opt-in entrance/exit animation for the overlay, via `nib_motion`.

members.name: transition

members.name: controller

required for basic use — `NibCommandPalette` creates and owns its own
controller when this is `null`. Pass an explicit instance to open the
palette from a trigger button elsewhere in the tree.

members.name: backgroundColor

members.name: hintStyle

Style of the [placeholder] hint in the search field. Merged onto the
default (which uses the theme's muted-foreground color).

members.name: defaultOpenShortcut

elsewhere.

components.name: NibCommandPaletteController

state and recent-action history. Never required for basic use —
`NibCommandPalette` creates and owns its own controller internally when
none is supplied, and disposes it on unmount/controller-swap. Pass an
explicit instance to open the palette from elsewhere in the tree (e.g. a

members.name: recentActionIds

occurrence first, then trims to [maxRecent].

components.name: NibContextMenu
components.documentation:
Wraps [child] so a right-click (desktop/web) or long-press (touch) opens a
context menu at the exact pointer/touch point, clamped to the viewport.

```dart
NibContextMenu(
  items: [
    NibMenuItem(label: 'Copy', icon: Icon(Icons.copy)),
    const NibMenuDivider(),
    NibMenuItem(label: 'Delete', destructive: true),
  ],
  onItemSelected: (item) => print(item.label),
  child: const Card(child: SizedBox(width: 200, height: 120)),
)
```

Submenus (a [NibMenuItem] with a `submenu`) open to the side; keyboard
navigation (↑/↓ move, →/Enter open/activate, ←/Esc back) works once open.

Opt-in enter animation via `nib_motion`. `false` builds zero `NibMotion`

members.name: label
members.documentation: The header label.

members.name: cellBuilder
members.documentation: Builds each row's cell content for this column.

members.documentation:
If set, this column's header can be tapped to sort by it, using this
as the comparison key. If `null`, this column is not sortable.

Also weights this column's share of flexible space relative to other flexible
columns — a column with a larger [minWidth] gets proportionally more flex space.
Only a true floor once the viewport is too narrow to fit every column's
[minWidth] — [NibDataTable] then switches to horizontal scrolling instead of
compressing columns below it.

components.name: NibDatePicker
components.documentation:
A native calendar / date picker with single, range, and multi-date
selection, month + year quick navigation, min/max bounds, a disabled-day
predicate, locale-aware labels, and three display modes: [inline],
[popover], and [dialog].

Simplest usage is an inline single-date calendar:

```dart
NibDatePicker(onDateChanged: (day) => print(day))
```

components.name: NibDialog
components.documentation:
Declarative face of the dialog, matching the house style of `NibSelect` /
`NibDatePicker`: a [trigger] whose tap opens a modal, with open/closed state
managed internally (or via an optional [controller]). Built on the same
[openNibDialog] primitive as [showNibDialog].

Simplest usage needs only [trigger] and [content]:

```dart
NibDialog(
  trigger: const Text('Open'),
  title: 'Details',
  content: const Text('…'),
)
```

The [trigger] is wrapped so a tap opens the dialog — pass a non-interactive
widget (text, icon, a custom chip). For a fire-and-forget confirm dialog
that returns a result, prefer [showNibDialog] instead.

members.signature:

    this.transition,
    this.onClose,

Optional external open/closed controller. Never required — `NibDialog`
creates and owns one internally when this is `null`, disposing it on
unmount/controller-swap.

Predefined entrance/exit motions for a dialog surface, layered on top of
`nib_motion`. Only used when `animated: true`; the timing/curve/spring is
controlled separately by the `transition` parameter.

members.documentation:

components.documentation:
Optional external controller for a `NibDialog`'s open/closed state. Never
required for basic use — `NibDialog` creates and owns its own controller
internally when none is supplied, and disposes it on unmount/controller-swap.

Pass an explicit instance to open/close the dialog from elsewhere in the
tree (e.g. a menu item or a keyboard shortcut). For the imperative
[showNibDialog] entry point there is no controller — its returned
`Future`/`NibDialogHandle` plays that role instead.

members.name: close

components.documentation:
A handle to an open dialog returned by [openNibDialog]. [showNibDialog]
hands back its [closed] future directly; the declarative `NibDialog` widget
keeps the whole handle so it can [close] the dialog when its controller flips.

Completes with the dialog's result when it closes (`null` if dismissed via

Exposes the enclosing dialog's [close] callback to its `content`/`footer`
subtree, so a button inside the dialog can dismiss it (optionally with a
result) without the consumer wiring a controller:

```dart
NibButton(
  label: 'Confirm',
  onPressed: () => NibDialogScope.of(context).close(true),
)
```

Preset max-width for a [showNibDialog]/`NibDialog` surface. The actual width
is clamped to the viewport minus a margin, so these are ceilings, not fixed
widths — a narrow phone still gets a full-bleed-minus-margin dialog.

members.documentation: ~380 logical px ceiling — alerts, confirmations.

members.name: md
members.documentation: ~512 logical px ceiling — the default; forms, standard content.

components.name: NibFlipCard
components.documentation:
A card that flips between [front] and [back] faces, 3D-rotated around
either the vertical or horizontal axis (via `nib_motion`'s [NibFlip]).

A distinct widget from [NibCard] — a flip card's whole identity is the
two-face flip contract ([front]/[back]/[flipAxis]/[isFlipped]), which
doesn't overlap with a plain card's header/footer/content slots.

Uncontrolled by default (tap either face to flip, like an
expand/collapse toggle): just supply [front]/[back]. Pass [isFlipped] +
[onFlippedChanged] for external control (the widget never mutates itself
once controlled — same `expanded: bool?` pattern as `NibAccordion`).

```dart
NibFlipCard(front: Text('Question'), back: Text('Answer'))

bool showBack = false;
NibFlipCard(
  front: const Text('Question'),
  back: const Text('Answer'),
  isFlipped: showBack,
  onFlippedChanged: (v) => setState(() => showBack = v),
)
```

members.name: NibFlipCard
members.signature:
const NibFlipCard({
    super.key,
    required this.front,
    required this.back,
    this.isFlipped,
    this.onFlippedChanged,
    this.flipAxis = Axis.horizontal,
    this.duration,
    this.tappable = true,
    this.padding,
    this.borderRadius,
    this.frontColor,
    this.backColor,
    this.borderColor,
    this.frontSemanticLabel,
    this.backSemanticLabel,

updates.

Which axis the card rotates around. [Axis.horizontal] rotates around

Whether tapping a face flips the card. Defaults to true; set false to
