components.name: NibHoverCard
components.documentation:
A native anchored hover card: a [trigger] that reveals a floating [content]
panel when the pointer hovers over it, and hides it again shortly after the
pointer leaves. Positioning reuses the shared `NibAnchoredOverlay` core
(auto-flip + viewport clamp) — the same primitive `NibPopover` uses.

Built for desktop/web hover, it degrades gracefully on touch: tapping the
trigger toggles the card (disable with [openOnTap]`: false`), and an outside
tap dismisses a tap-opened card. Unlike a modal, it never dims the app or
**steals focus** from the trigger — hovering onto the card itself keeps it
open, so the content stays reachable.

Simplest usage needs only [trigger] and [content]:

```dart
NibHoverCard(
  trigger: Text('@flutter'),
  content: Text('The Flutter team account.'),
)
```

[showDelay]/[hideDelay] tune the hover-intent timing so quick pass-overs
don't flicker the card. Drive it programmatically with a [controller].

members.name: NibHoverCard
members.signature:
const NibHoverCard({
    super.key,
    this.trigger,
    this.controller,
    required this.content,
    this.placement = NibHoverCardPlacement.bottom,
    this.showDelay = const Duration(milliseconds: 700),
    this.hideDelay = const Duration(milliseconds: 300),
    this.gap = 8,
    this.maxWidth = 320,
    this.openOnTap = true,
    this.animated = false,
    this.transition,
    this.enterFrom,
    this.onOpen,
    this.onClose,
    this.semanticLabel,
  })

The widget the pointer hovers over to reveal the card. Optional — omit and
drive via [controller].

owns one internally when this is `null`, disposing it on
unmount/controller-swap. Hover/tap intent still drives it when present.

How long the pointer must rest on the trigger before the card opens. Tuned
so a quick pass-over doesn't flash the card.

closes. The grace period lets the pointer cross the [gap] onto the card
without it closing.

components.documentation:
Optional external controller for a `NibHoverCard`'s open/closed state. Never
required for basic use — `NibHoverCard` creates and owns one internally when
none is supplied, and disposes it on unmount/controller-swap.

Pass an explicit instance to open/close the card from elsewhere in the tree,
or to read whether it is currently showing. Hover/tap intent still drives it
automatically when present.

Which side of the trigger a [NibHoverCard] prefers to open toward. Flips to

components.name: NibInput
components.documentation:
A native, token-driven single-line text field.

Simple by default — `NibInput(onChanged: ...)` already looks finished —
with optional [label]/[helperText]/[errorText] chrome, leading/trailing
icon slots, and a built-in [clearable] button.

Extends [FormField], so it works inside a Flutter [Form] exactly like
[TextFormField] does: `Form(key: formKey, child: Column(children: [
NibInput(validator: ...), ...]))`, then `formKey.currentState!.validate()`
/ `.save()` / `.reset()`.

```dart
NibInput(label: 'Email', placeholder: 'you@example.com', onChanged: (v) {})
NibInput(prefixIcon: Icon(Icons.search), clearable: true, onChanged: (v) {})
NibInput(
  label: 'Email',
  validator: NibValidators.compose([NibValidators.required(), NibValidators.email()]),
)
```

components.name: NibLiquidGlass
components.documentation:
A "liquid glass" container — Apple's Liquid Glass material as a Flutter box.

Built on `nib_motion`'s [NibGlass] engine (which models the glass as a
[thickness]-px-deep dome and bends the backdrop through it with real
Snell's-law refraction — plus chromatic dispersion, a saturation boost and
background-derived rim lighting — via the bundled `liquid_glass.frag`
shader on Impeller, and falls back to a frosted blur +
painted rim elsewhere). This component adds the
ergonomic layer: `NibTheme` token defaults, an [interactive] mode where the
specular highlight tracks the pointer and a press gives a subtle scale (via
`nib_motion`, under the [animated] contract), and full shape control through
[borderRadius] or a custom [clipper].

Simplest usage wraps any content over a busy background:

```dart
NibLiquidGlass(
  child: Padding(padding: EdgeInsets.all(20), child: Text('Glass')),
)
```

listen), and drive it with [setValue]/[clear] — e.g. to prefill a code or to
reset the field after a failed verification.

components.name: NibOtpInput
components.documentation:
A one-time-code / PIN entry field: a row of [length] single-character cells
that fill as the user types, auto-advancing per digit.

Built on a single native [TextField] behind the cells, so the hard parts
come for free: **pasting** a whole code splits it across the cells, and
**SMS autofill** works via [AutofillHints.oneTimeCode]. Digits only by
default. Usable with just a length:

```dart
NibOtpInput(length: 6, onCompleted: (code) => verify(code))
```

Drive/read it with a [NibOtpController]; set [obscureText] to mask entries,
[errorText] to show an error state, and [animated] to pop each cell in via
`nib_motion`.

A page navigator with ellipsis collapsing for large page counts.

inherits focus, keyboard activation and tap-target sizing for free.

```dart
  onPageChanged: (p) => setState(() => page = p))

  variant: NibPaginationVariant.compact, onPageChanged: ...)
```

components.name: NibPopover
components.documentation:
A native anchored popover: a [trigger] whose tap opens a floating [content]
panel positioned next to it, auto-flipping and clamping to the viewport via
the shared `NibAnchoredOverlay` positioning core (the same primitive
`NibSelect`/`NibNavigationMenu` build on). Non-modal — it doesn't trap focus
or dim the app; an outside tap dismisses it unless [dismissOnOutsideTap] is
`false` (then close via a [controller] or [NibPopoverScope]).

Simplest usage needs only [trigger] and [content]:

```dart
NibPopover(
  trigger: const Icon(Icons.info_outline),
  content: const Text('More info'),
)
```

The [trigger] is wrapped in a tap handler that toggles the popover — pass a
non-interactive widget (text, icon, a custom chip). Drive it externally with
a [controller] when you need to.

    this.showArrow = false,

Whether an outside tap dismisses the popover. `false` keeps it open until
closed via a [controller] or [NibPopoverScope] (an invisible tap-catching

`false` and the only way to close is programmatic.

components.documentation:
A single-select group of radio options with roving-tabindex keyboard
navigation — one tab stop for the whole group, arrow keys move (and
select) between options, matching native `<input type="radio">` groups.

Controlled, like [NibTheme]'s other inputs: the group's entire state is
its [value], already owned by the [value]/[onChanged] pair, so there is
no separate controller.

```dart
NibRadioGroup<String>(
  options: const [
    NibRadioOption(value: 'a', label: 'Alpha'),
    NibRadioOption(value: 'b', label: 'Beta'),
  ],
  value: selected,
  onChanged: (v) => setState(() => selected = v),
)
```

One panel in a `NibResizablePanels` group.

[minSize]/[maxSize]/[initialSize] are fractions (`0.0`–`1.0`) of the
group's own main-axis extent, not pixels — this keeps the layout correct
across window/viewport resizes without reconciling absolute pixel bounds
against a shrinking or growing container.

Creates a panel. If [initialSize] is omitted, this panel shares the
fraction left over after every panel with an explicit [initialSize] is
accounted for, split evenly among the other omitted panels.

members.name: minSize
members.documentation:
The minimum fraction (of the group's main-axis extent) this panel can
be resized to. Defaults to `0.1` (10%).

members.name: maxSize
members.documentation:
The maximum fraction this panel can be resized to. Defaults to `1.0`
(100%) — effectively unbounded, since the other panels' own minimums
prevent any single panel from actually reaching it.

members.name: initialSize
members.documentation:
This panel's starting fraction of the group. `null` shares the
remaining space evenly with every other panel that also omits it.

components.name: NibResizablePanels
components.documentation:
A horizontal or vertical group of resizable panels with draggable,
keyboard-resizable, min/max-constrained dividers between them.

```dart
NibResizablePanels(
  direction: Axis.horizontal,
  panels: [
    NibResizablePanel(child: Sidebar()),
    NibResizablePanel(child: MainContent()),
  ],
)
```

Must be given bounded constraints in both axes (e.g. wrap it in a
`SizedBox` or `Expanded` within a bounded parent).

called (or whenever [panels]' length changes, e.g. a panel was added or
removed). A no-op if [sizes] is already seeded at the same length, so
it's safe to call on every `NibResizablePanels` build without

components.name: NibSelect
components.documentation:
A native single/multi select: a button-style trigger that opens an
anchored, keyboard-navigable dropdown of [NibSelectOption]s. The overlay
flips above the trigger and clamps its height to the available space when
there isn't room below, matches the trigger's width, supports optional
in-list search, grouped section headers ([groups]), and disabled options.

Simplest usage needs only [options] and [onChanged]:

```dart
NibSelect<String>(
  options: const [
    NibSelectOption(value: 'apple', label: 'Apple'),
    NibSelectOption(value: 'banana', label: 'Banana'),
  ],
  onChanged: (value) => print(value),
)
```

Pass [groups] instead of [options] for grouped section headers; the two are
mutually exclusive.

members.name: options
members.documentation:
The flat, ungrouped option list — the common case. Mutually exclusive
with [groups].

members.name: groups
members.documentation:
Grouped options rendered with a section header per group. Mutually
exclusive with [options].

members.name: value
members.documentation:
Initial single-select value, applied to the internally-owned controller
on first build. Ignored when an external [controller] is supplied (that
controller is the source of truth).

members.name: values
members.documentation:
Initial multi-select values, applied to the internally-owned controller
on first build. Ignored when an external [controller] is supplied.

members.name: multiSelect
members.documentation:
Multi-select mode: picks toggle, the dropdown stays open, and the closed
trigger shows the selected labels joined with commas (ellipsised).

members.name: searchable
members.documentation:
Whether to show an in-list search field at the top of the dropdown that
filters options by label/subtitle.

members.name: clearable
members.documentation:
Whether to show a trailing clear (✕) button on the trigger when there's a
selection to clear.

members.name: onChanged
members.documentation:
Single-select convenience: fires the newly-selected value (or `null` when
cleared). For multi-select use [onSelectionChanged].

members.name: onSelectionChanged
members.documentation: Fires the full selection list on every selection change, in both modes.

members.name: noResultsBuilder
members.documentation:
Builds the dropdown body when [searchable] has filtered options to none.
Defaults to a muted "No results" row.

members.name: loading
members.documentation:
Consumer-forced loading state — shows a spinner in the dropdown body in
place of the option list.

members.name: animated
members.documentation:
Opt-in dropdown entrance/exit animation via `nib_motion`. `false`
allocates zero `NibMotion`/`NibPresence`/`MotionValue` overhead (the
dropdown appears and closes instantly).

members.name: animation
members.documentation:
Which predefined motion the dropdown opens/closes with when [animated] is
`true`. Ignored when [enterFrom] is set (that raw state wins) or when
[animated] is `false`. Defaults to [NibSelectAnimation.fadeScale].

members.name: enterFrom
members.documentation:
Raw escape hatch: the [NibAnim] "from" state the dropdown animates out of
on open and back into on close, overriding [animation]. Only used when
[animated] is `true`.

members.name: staggerOptions
members.documentation:
When `true` (and [animated] is `true`), each option row animates in
staggered (a cascade) instead of the whole panel moving as one block.
This builds all visible rows eagerly (no `ListView` virtualization), so
it's intended for modest option counts — leave it `false` for very long
lists.

members.name: transition
members.documentation:
Timing/curve/spring for the [animated] transition (both directions).
`null` falls back to a short ~140ms ease. The motion *shape* comes from
[animation]/[enterFrom]; this only controls how it's timed.

members.name: semanticLabel
members.documentation: Overrides the trigger's accessibility label. Defaults to [placeholder].

members.name: controller
members.documentation:
Optional external controller for selection/open state. Never required —
`NibSelect` creates and owns one internally when this is `null`, and
disposes it on unmount/controller-swap.

members.name: backgroundColor
members.documentation:
Fill color of the trigger (and the dropdown card, so both read as one
surface). `null` ⇒ [NibTheme.background] for the trigger (or
[NibTheme.muted] while [disabled]) and [NibTheme.card] for the dropdown.

members.name: borderColor
members.documentation:
Border color of the trigger. `null` ⇒ [NibTheme.ring] while open,
otherwise [NibTheme.border].

members.name: borderWidth
members.documentation: Border thickness of the trigger. `null` ⇒ `1`.

members.name: borderRadius
members.documentation: Corner radius of the trigger. `null` ⇒ [NibTheme.radiusDefault].

members.name: padding
members.documentation: Inner content padding of the trigger. `null` ⇒ a sensible default.

members.name: minHeight
members.documentation:
Minimum height of the closed trigger. Defaults to 46 logical pixels.
The trigger can grow when its contents need more room.

members.name: placeholderStyle
members.documentation:
Style of the [placeholder] text shown on the trigger while nothing is
selected. Merged onto the default (which uses [NibTheme.mutedForeground]).

components.name: NibSelectAnimation
components.documentation:
Predefined entrance/exit motions for a [NibSelect] dropdown, layered on top
of `nib_motion`. Pick one via `NibSelect.animation` (only used when
`animated: true`); the timing/curve/spring is still controlled separately
by `NibSelect.transition`.

Each preset is direction-aware — a `slide`/`slideFade` opening *upward*
(when there's no room below the trigger) slides from below instead of
above. For full control, bypass the enum with `NibSelect.enterFrom` (a raw
[NibAnim] "from" state).

members.name: none
members.documentation:
No entrance transform — the dropdown simply appears (and closes
instantly). Equivalent to `animated: false` for the dropdown itself.

members.name: fade
members.documentation: Fade opacity in on open, out on close.

members.name: slide
members.documentation: Translate from the trigger edge (no opacity change).

members.name: scale
members.documentation: Scale up from slightly small (no translation).

members.name: fadeScale
members.documentation: Fade + a small scale-up. The default when `animated: true`.

members.name: slideFade
members.documentation: Fade + a slide from the trigger edge.

components.name: NibSelectController
components.documentation:
Optional external controller for a [NibSelect]'s selection and open/closed
state. Never required for basic use — `NibSelect` creates and owns its own
controller internally when none is supplied, and disposes it on
unmount/controller-swap. Pass an explicit instance to read or drive the
select from elsewhere in the tree (e.g. a "clear" button, or reading the
current selection for a form).

members.name: selectedValues
members.documentation:
The currently-selected values, in selection order (a single-element list
in single-select mode). Unmodifiable — mutate via [selectOnly] /
[toggle] / [clear].

members.name: selectedValue
members.documentation:
Convenience accessor for single-select use: the first selected value, or
`null` if nothing is selected.

members.name: isOpen
members.documentation: Whether the dropdown is currently open.

members.name: selectOnly
members.documentation: Replaces the whole selection with just [value] (single-select semantics).

members.name: toggle
members.documentation: Adds [value] if absent, removes it if present (multi-select semantics).

members.name: clear
members.documentation: Clears the whole selection.

members.name: setSelection
members.documentation:
Replaces the whole selection with [values] (used to seed an initial
selection). No-op if it already equals the current selection.

components.name: NibSelectGroup
components.documentation:
A labelled section of [options] in a [NibSelect].

Passed via `NibSelect.groups` (mutually exclusive with the flat
`NibSelect.options`) to render section headers above each group's rows —
the ungrouped common case stays a plain flat `options` list.

members.name: label
members.documentation: The section-header text shown above this group's [options].

components.name: NibSelectNoResultsBuilder
components.documentation:
Builds the dropdown body shown when a `searchable` [NibSelect] has filtered
its options down to nothing.

components.name: NibSelectOption
components.documentation:
One selectable entry in a [NibSelect].

[value] is the typed payload reported through the change callbacks and the
controller; [label] is the human-readable text shown in the dropdown row,
joined into the closed trigger once selected, and matched against by the
in-list search when `searchable` is on.

bone/skeleton version of it instead of a hand-rebuilt parallel skeleton
tree — see `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-18-skeleton-design.md` for the
detection algorithm.

```dart

  loading: isLoading,
  animated: true,
  child: ProfileHeader(user: user),
)
```

Extra gap inserted between each pair of consecutive children in a

renders [child] normally — the same "one authored tree" rule every other
spot in a `NibSkeleton` follows.

components.name: NibSlider

A native, token-driven slider with an optional two-thumb range mode.

Simple by default — `NibSlider(value: v, onChanged: ...)` — with opt-in tick

full geometry/colour escape hatches. Animation is opt-in ([animated]); the
drag and track-fill always follow the pointer 1:1.

```dart
  onChanged: ...)
NibSlider.range(values: price, onChanged: (r) => setState(() => price = r))
```

components.name: NibSwitch
components.documentation:
A boolean on/off switch with an optional [loading] state for
async-confirmed toggles (tap fires [onChanged], but the switch stays busy
— thumb shows a spinner, interaction blocked — until the consumer settles
[value]/[loading] once the change is confirmed).

```dart
NibSwitch(value: wifiOn, onChanged: (v) => setState(() => wifiOn = v))
NibSwitch(
  value: syncing,
  loading: confirming,
  label: 'Sync',
  onChanged: (v) async {
    setState(() => confirming = true);
    final ok = await api.setSync(v);
    setState(() { confirming = false; if (ok) syncing = v; });
  },
)
NibSwitch(
  value: isDark,
  animated: true,
  onThumbIcon: Image.asset('assets/images/moon.png'),
  offThumbIcon: Image.asset('assets/images/sun.png'),
  onChanged: (v) => setState(() => isDark = v),
)
```

components.name: NibTabs
components.documentation:
A tab set that solves the two things "floater tabs" get wrong:

1. **No stuck scroll.** `NibTabs` owns exactly one vertical scroll (an
   internal [CustomScrollView]): your [header] scrolls away, the bar pins, the
   active panel scrolls as part of that *same* scroll, then your [footer]
   scrolls in. Because the panel is not its own [Scrollable], reaching its end
   just keeps scrolling the page — it can never trap the user.
2. **A gutter between panels.** Swiping (or tapping) from one tab to the next
   separates the outgoing and incoming panels by [panelGap] so they never look
   glued together, and the pager height reflows smoothly between panels of
   different heights.

**Contract:** put "content above" in [header] and "content below" in [footer];
do **not** wrap `NibTabs` in another vertical `ListView`/`SingleChildScrollView`
— that reintroduces the nested-scroll bug this widget exists to prevent.
`NibTabs` expects a bounded height (it fills its parent, like any scroll view).

```dart
NibTabs(
  header: MyHero(),
  tabs: [
    NibTab(label: 'Posts', builder: (_) => PostsList()),
    NibTab(label: 'About', builder: (_) => AboutPanel()),
  ],
  footer: MyFooter(),
)
```

A native, token-driven multi-line text field.

growing from [minLines] up to [maxLines] as the user types (then
scrolling), with optional [label]/[helperText]/[errorText]/character
counter chrome.

[TextFormField] does: `Form(key: formKey, child: Column(children: [

/ `.save()` / `.reset()`.

components.name: NibToaster
components.documentation:
Wrap your app once (typically via `MaterialApp.builder`) so [showNibToast]
works anywhere without a `context`:

```dart
MaterialApp(
  builder: (context, child) => NibToaster(child: child!),
  home: HomePage(),
);
```

It hosts its own [Overlay] (with the app as the base layer) and registers it
with the toast controller, so toasts float above the whole app. Since
`MaterialApp.builder` sits *above* the Navigator's overlay, `NibToaster`
supplies one there itself rather than borrowing an ancestor's.

components.name: NibToggleGroup
components.documentation:
A row of segments where one ([NibToggleGroup.new]) or several
([NibToggleGroup.multiple]) can be pressed at once — each segment is a
[NibButton], so it inherits focus/ripple/tap-target/semantics for free.

Roving-tabindex keyboard model: the group has **one** tab stop; arrow
keys move focus between segments (wrapping past the ends, skipping
disabled ones) without changing selection, and Enter/Space/tap toggles
the focused segment — matching a native toolbar's toggle-button group,
not a radio group (arrows don't auto-select here).

```dart
NibToggleGroup<String>(
  options: const [
    NibToggleOption(value: 'left', icon: Icon(Icons.format_align_left)),
    NibToggleOption(value: 'center', icon: Icon(Icons.format_align_center)),
  ],
  value: align,
  onChanged: (v) => setState(() => align = v),
)
NibToggleGroup<String>.multiple(
  options: const [
    NibToggleOption(value: 'bold', label: 'B'),
    NibToggleOption(value: 'italic', label: 'I'),
  ],
  values: activeStyles,
  onChanged: (v) => setState(() => activeStyles = v),
)
```

components.name: breadcrumbVisibleIndices
components.documentation:
The visible crumb positions for a trail of [count] items, given whether it is
[collapsed]. `null` entries mark the ellipsis/overflow slot; ints are item
indices.

When collapsed, the first [before] and last [after] items are kept and the
middle is replaced by a single ellipsis. Never collapses a trail of
`count <= before + after`.

```dart
breadcrumbVisibleIndices(count: 5, collapsed: true);  // [0, null, 4]
breadcrumbVisibleIndices(count: 5, collapsed: false); // [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]
```

components.documentation:

components.name: kNibResizablePanelsNarrowFallbackPanelExtent
components.documentation:
Below `panels.length * kNibResizablePanelsNarrowFallbackPanelExtent`
logical pixels along the main axis, `NibResizablePanels` renders a
scrollable, handle-less stack of full-size panels instead of squishing
them below a usable size (master prompt §1.7).

The fallback always stacks **vertically** and scrolls vertically,
regardless of `direction` — for a `vertical` group this is the same axis
it already uses (it just gains scrolling instead of squishing); for a
`horizontal` group this is a deliberate axis pivot, collapsing
side-by-side panels into a single scrollable column (the locked
brainstorming decision — see the design doc's "Narrow-viewport fallback"
section — not merely making the horizontal row scroll sideways).

components.documentation:

`[kNibSheetMinExtent, 1.0]`.

the sheet as content-sized with a single implicit snap and drag-to-dismiss
only.

components.name: paginationRange
components.documentation:
Computes the visible page slots for a numbered pagination, collapsing large
gaps into ellipses. `null` entries mark an ellipsis; ints are page numbers.

A port of MUI's `usePagination` item algorithm: [boundaryCount] pages are
pinned at each end, [siblingCount] pages are shown either side of
[currentPage], and a gap of a single page is shown as that page (never an
ellipsis for just one number).

```dart
paginationRange(currentPage: 5, totalPages: 10); // [1, null, 4, 5, 6, null, 10]
paginationRange(currentPage: 1, totalPages: 10); // [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, null, 10]
```

components.name: showNibAlertDialog
components.documentation:
Imperative confirm/alert popup — Flutter's `AlertDialog` equivalent, built
on [showNibDialog]: a modal with a title/message and Cancel/OK actions
that returns a result.

```dart
final confirmed = await showNibAlertDialog(
  context,
  title: 'Delete file?',
  description: 'This cannot be undone.',
  severity: NibAlertSeverity.error,
);
if (confirmed == true) { ... }
```

Resolves `true` when [confirmText] is tapped, `false` when [cancelText]
is tapped, `null` when dismissed via the barrier/Escape without deciding.
Pass `cancelText: null` for a single-button informational alert. There is
no corner close button — matching Flutter's own `AlertDialog`, dismissal
is always via an explicit action or the barrier, never a redundant second
affordance next to Cancel.

[icon]/[iconColor]/[titleTextStyle]/[descriptionTextStyle] customize the
body beyond [severity]'s defaults; [actionsAlignment]/[actionsSpacing]/
[actionsOverflowAlignment]/[actionsOverflowDirection] tune the action row
(backed by [OverflowBar], so it wraps to a vertical stack instead of
overflowing when actions don't fit — matters most with a custom
multi-button [actions] override).

The default Cancel/OK pair is itself fully customizable: [cancelVariant]/
[confirmVariant] pick each button's [NibButtonVariant] (e.g. set both to
the same variant if two visually different button styles — outline next
to filled — don't read as a matched pair at your chosen [buttonPadding]/
text lengths), [buttonPadding] overrides both buttons' internal padding,
[buttonWidth] forces both to an identical width (the most direct fix when
two different-length labels, like "Cancel"/"Delete", produce visibly
different content-sized button widths), and [cancelFirst] controls left-
to-right order (`true`, the default, is Cancel-then-Confirm). All of
these — including [actionsAlignment] etc. above — are Material-only;
[adaptive]'s iOS presentation uses fixed native-style full-width actions
instead ([buttonPadding] and [cancelFirst] still apply there; variant/
width/alignment do not, since Cupertino actions have no discrete width or
[NibButtonVariant] concept).

Set [adaptive] to switch to an iOS-style presentation (centered text,
full-width divided text actions, no ripple) when running on iOS/macOS;
`false` (the default) always uses the Material-style layout regardless of
platform.

components.name: showNibToast
components.documentation:
Shows a toast over the root [Overlay] and returns its id (use it with
[dismissNibToast]). Toasts stack at their [position] and auto-dismiss after
[duration] (`Duration.zero` keeps it until dismissed).

**Context-free:** wrap your app in a [NibToaster] (e.g. via
`MaterialApp.builder`) and you can call `showNibToast(...)` from anywhere —
a service, a bloc, a callback — with no `context`. If you don't use a
[NibToaster], pass a [context] that has an [Overlay] ancestor.

Passing an [id] that is already showing applies [onDuplicateTrigger] instead
of stacking a duplicate — by default the existing toast [NibToastDuplicateBehavior.shake]s.

Shape it with [padding], [borderRadius], and [backgroundColor] (handy when
supplying your own [content]).

```dart
showNibToast(
  title: 'Saved',
  variant: NibToastVariant.success,
  animated: true,
);
```
